BHP.title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: BHP directors, employees and contractors
tiers.description: Everyone the policy applies to. Subject only to the insider trading and confidentiality prohibitions and the substance-over-form approach; no clearance or closed-period obligation unless they fall in a tier below.

tiers.name: Persons on insider lists
tiers.description: People recorded on a BHP insider list maintained by Group Governance. Must request clearance from the Group Company Secretary before dealing and must not deal during any Closed Period.

tiers.name: Participants in BHP's employee incentive plans
tiers.description: Participants in the Cash and Deferred Plan, Long Term Incentive Plan, Management Award Plan, Short-Term Incentive Plan or successors (excluding Shareplus). Must not deal in any Closed Period and must never hedge unvested or holding-locked plan securities. No clearance requirement in this capacity.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: People who regularly have access to sensitive BHP information: non-PDMR Executive Leadership Team members, their assistants and managers, Investor Relations, Group Governance, Asset Presidents, key Corporate Affairs and Group Reporting employees. Clearance required; no dealing in Closed Periods.

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Persons Discharging Managerial Responsibilities: directors of BHP Group Limited, Key Management Personnel named in the Remuneration Report, and anyone the Group Company Secretary determines to be a PDMR. Clearance required, no dealing in Closed Periods, plus express bans on short-term dealing, short selling, exchange-traded derivatives and using unvested securities as collateral; post-trade notification to the Group Company Secretary, FCA and exchanges.

tiers.name: PCAs
tiers.description: Persons Closely Associated with a PDMR: spouse/civil partner, dependent children and stepchildren, relatives sharing the household for a year, and companies, trusts, partnerships or entities managed or controlled by, set up for the benefit of, or economically equivalent to a PDMR or family member. Must obtain clearance (the PDMR may submit the form) and must not deal in Closed Periods; PDMR must notify them and obtain acknowledgement.

BHP.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Disclosure Committee may declare any other period a Closed Period. The policy is silent on whether such a declaration is confidential.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on put options, call options or other derivative securities dealt on an exchange or in any other organised market, regardless of the state of the underlying shares.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market

rules.detail: The express derivatives ban is venue-limited to exchanges and organised markets. A bilateral OTC put and call with a bank falls outside it but is a dealing (contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations; grant/acceptance of an option; 'securities' includes financial products whether quoted or not), so it requires clearance from the Group Company Secretary, cannot occur in a Closed Period, and must not have a maturity of one year or less. Substance over form applies.
rules.evidence: entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations; the grant, acceptance, acquisition, disposal, exercise or discharge of any option

rules.detail: Any derivative that uses unvested securities as collateral is caught by the PDMR collateral ban, which expressly includes hedging.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule for Restricted Persons or persons on insider lists; options and price-referenced contracts are dealings requiring clearance and barred in Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: must request clearance before dealing in BHP securities from the Group Company Secretary in BHP securities by submitting a Securities Dealing Clearance Request Form

rules.detail: For staff outside the restricted tiers, derivatives are dealings subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the reputational guiding principle.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to or interest in securities

rules.tier: Participants in BHP's employee incentive plans
rules.detail: Absolute, at-any-time ban on any transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit exposure to the risk of holding unvested plan securities.
rules.evidence: Participants must not at any time enter into a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit participants' exposure to the risk of holding unvested BHP securities granted under a BHP employee incentive plan

rules.tier: Participants in BHP's employee incentive plans
rules.detail: The hedging ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to holding locks or similar restrictions.
rules.evidence: or vested BHP securities that are subject to holding locks or similar restrictions.

rules.detail: PDMRs may not use unvested securities as collateral in any financial transaction, expressly including hedging.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted shares is not expressly banned for PDMRs. It is a dealing requiring clearance, outside Closed Periods, not via exchange-traded derivatives, and not with a maturity of one year or less. Clearance is discretionary and will be refused where the dealing could be perceived as taking advantage of position.
rules.evidence: Where clearance is required for a dealing under this policy, clearance will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the considerations above.

rules.detail: For non-plan-participant, non-restricted staff, hedging vested unrestricted shares is not named; it is a dealing subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose, a price-referenced contract and (if funded) a secured financing arrangement, all of which are dealings requiring clearance and post-trade notification. Structures with a maturity of one year or less are short-term dealings and prohibited.
rules.evidence: any application for, acquisition or disposal of, or agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities

rules.detail: Same dealing-definition analysis; clearance required, no short-term or derivatives restrictions beyond Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of securities

rules.detail: Express ban on short selling, defined as borrowing and selling in the hope of buying back lower.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves short selling BHP securities (i.e. the practice of borrowing a security and selling it in the hope that it can be bought back at a lower price some time in the future to close out the short position)

rules.detail: Not expressly banned for non-PDMRs; a short sale and the associated stock loan are dealings requiring clearance for Restricted Persons and insider-list persons.
rules.evidence: entry into, termination of, assignment of, or novation of any stock lending agreement

rules.detail: Not banned, but entry into, termination, assignment or novation of a stock lending agreement is a dealing requiring clearance and post-trade notification.
rules.evidence: entry into, termination of, assignment of, or novation of any stock lending agreement

rules.detail: Stock lending is a dealing requiring clearance and barred in Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: entry into, termination of, assignment of, or novation of any stock lending agreement

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations and so a dealing requiring clearance; if it is traded on an exchange or organised market it falls within the express derivatives ban, a short CFD is likely within the short selling ban in substance, and an open-ended CFD held short-term may be a short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Express ban on margin loans collateralised by unvested securities.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements

rules.detail: Margin lending over vested securities is not banned but entry into the arrangement is expressly a dealing, so it needs clearance, cannot be entered in a Closed Period, and must be notified post-trade (and by BHP to the FCA and exchanges).
rules.evidence: entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Entry into a margin lending arrangement is a dealing requiring clearance for Restricted Persons and insider-list persons.
rules.evidence: entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: For general staff a margin loan is a dealing subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities is itself a dealing, so a security interest over the collared shares needs clearance, is barred in Closed Periods and triggers PDMR post-trade notification.
rules.evidence: use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities

rules.detail: Using unvested securities as collateral in any financial transaction is banned.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: Granting an encumbrance is a dealing requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities

rules.detail: No financial transaction may be collateralised by unvested securities.
rules.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement (not just margin loans) is a dealing; permitted for vested unrestricted shares with clearance, outside Closed Periods, with post-trade notification to the Group Company Secretary and onward FCA/exchange disclosure. The policy is silent on holding-locked vested shares as collateral for a loan, though hedging them is banned for plan participants.
rules.evidence: entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Secured financing is a dealing requiring clearance for Restricted Persons and insider-list persons.
rules.evidence: entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Instrument-maturity test: any investment with a maturity of one year or less is short-term and prohibited. A collar or loan with tenor of 12 months or less is caught.
rules.evidence: on a short-term basis. An investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered of a short-term nature

The Board or Disclosure Committee declares additional Closed Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited from dealing ... where the dealing involves transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bilateral OTC collar with a bank is outside the express ban, so its treatment turns on the dealing definition and clearance, but the bank should not hedge or novate the position through listed options in the executive's name.

bespoke_clauses.clause: BHP will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Clearance Officer may treat an OTC collar as within the spirit of the exchange-traded derivatives ban or the hedging ban and refuse clearance on that basis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered of a short-term nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the collar and the loan must have a tenor exceeding twelve months for a PDMR, and early termination or roll features may be scrutinised.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Participants must not at any time enter into a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit participants' exposure to the risk of holding unvested BHP securities ... or vested BHP securities that are subject to holding locks or similar restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only vested shares free of holding locks or plan restrictions can be collared; the ban applies at any time, including outside Closed Periods, and is intent-based.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing includes ... use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities ... entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg and the security interest over the collared shares each require clearance and are barred in Closed Periods, and for PDMRs are publicly disclosed via FCA and exchange notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived as taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? ... clearance will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the considerations above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for a director's collar is discretionary and may be refused on perception grounds even absent inside information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Upon receipt of written approval, the dealing must be completed within two business days. ... A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and loan must be priced and signed within two business days of clearance, and BHP can withdraw clearance before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs must ensure that their PCAs: must request clearance before dealing in BHP securities ... companies, trusts, partnerships or entities: which are managed by a PDMR or a family member; which are directly or indirectly controlled by a PDMR
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered through a family trust or controlled company needs the same clearance and disclosure as if entered by the PDMR.

bespoke_clauses.clause: exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial difficulty or compulsion by court order, exist which require the immediate sale of shares
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closed Period relief covers an immediate sale, not entry into a hedge or financing, and the policy is silent on a lender's enforcement sale in a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: dealing on behalf of a third party
bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons on insider lists, Restricted Persons, PDMRs and their PCAs must not deal (or deal on behalf of a third party) in BHP securities during any Closed Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement, unwind or collateral top-up during a Closed Period would be a dealing; structures should cash-settle or avoid mandatory delivery dates in Closed Periods.

BHP.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is possible for a BHP PDMR (director or KMP) but only with prior written clearance from the Group Company Secretary, executed within two business days of clearance, outside Closed Periods (year-end and half-year-end to results, plus any Board or Disclosure Committee blackout) and with a tenor exceeding one year, since investments maturing in one year or less are prohibited short-term dealings. The express PDMR derivatives ban is limited to exchange-traded or organised-market instruments, so a bilateral OTC put and call is caught only as a dealing, though BHP applies a substance-over-form approach and clearance is discretionary. Unvested securities and vested securities under holding locks cannot be hedged or used as collateral at all, so only free vested shares can be collared or charged. The loan and the security interest over the shares are each dealings requiring clearance and, for PDMRs, post-trade notification to the Group Company Secretary with onward FCA and exchange disclosure. The policy is silent on forced sales by a lender in a Closed Period, and the exceptional-circumstances relief covers only an immediate sale.

CBA.title: Group Personal Trading Policy

tiers.name: all employees
tiers.description: All full-time, part-time and casual employees, contractors, secondees, and directors of CBA and its subsidiaries. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and by Pre-Clearance and other requirements in the Group Personal Trading Procedure where designated on the Conflicts Hub.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: Anyone likely to have access to price-sensitive Group information; at a minimum CBA Board directors, Group Executives, Subsidiary Board directors, Group and Subsidiary company secretaries, Executive General Managers, their direct support staff and Group Control Room employees. Designation is recorded on the Conflicts Hub and may change.

tiers.name: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
tiers.description: Sub-tier of Specified Persons subject to the wider hedging ban on any vested Group Securities (para 9), UK/EU MAR restrictions (para 18) and express Pre-Clearance requirements (para 4). All Specified Persons rules also apply to them.

rules.detail: No transaction limiting economic risk of exposure to unvested Group Securities received under a Group equity plan. Extends to Associates via para 17 and the definition of Specified Person obligations.

rules.evidence: vested but subject to a holding lock or trading restriction under the terms of the plan.

rules.detail: Para 8 is confined to unvested and locked plan securities, so a Specified Person outside the para 9 sub-tier (e.g. an Executive General Manager or Subsidiary Board director) is not expressly barred from hedging vested unrestricted shares. A collar is a derivative over Group Securities, hence a Security, and entering it is a Trade: it may only be done in a Trading Window, with Pre-Clearance where required under the Procedure, and subject to the 30-day LIFO holding rule and the CFD/short selling/stock lending bans.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Associates may only Trade in Group Securities during a Trading Window unless one of the exceptions below applies.

rules.tier: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
rules.detail: Absolute ban on risk-limiting transactions over any vested Group Securities, whether plan-sourced or bought on market; extends to Associates. A purchased put or collar over vested shares is caught.
rules.evidence: the CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives, and each of their Associates, must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities.

rules.tier: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
rules.detail: Caught by para 9 (any vested Group Securities) and by para 8(b) as Specified Persons.
rules.evidence: must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities.

rules.tier: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
rules.detail: Caught by para 8(a) as Specified Persons.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to Group Securities received under any Group equity plan that are: a. unvested

rules.detail: The hedging bans are confined to Specified Persons and the para 9 sub-tier; the policy is silent for other employees beyond the insider trading prohibition and any Procedure requirements.

Derivatives, including OTC options and hedges settled in cash or otherwise, are Securities; a derivative over Group Securities is a Group Security. Not banned as a class (other than CFDs and short selling/stock lending instruments) but may only be entered in a Trading Window with Pre-Clearance where required, and subject to the hedging bans in paras 8-9.
rules.evidence: any derivatives products relating to the types of securities listed above, including but not limited to equity swaps, warrants, futures, contracts for difference, hedges and exchange traded or over the counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.tier: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
rules.detail: Any derivative that limits economic risk on vested Group Securities (put, collar, swap) is barred by para 9; a derivative that does not limit risk is a Trade requiring a Trading Window and Pre-Clearance. Para 18(b) separately bans any Security whose price depends on a Group Security listed on a UK or EU regulated market.
rules.evidence: must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities.

rules.detail: Only the insider trading prohibition and any Pre-Clearance designated under the Procedure apply.

Monetisation is not named. An agreement to dispose, or a cash-settled derivative, is a Trade and so is confined to Trading Windows with Pre-Clearance where required. Monetisation through a secured loan is barred by para 16(a); monetisation of unvested or locked plan shares through a risk-limiting transaction is barred by para 8.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading includes buying, selling, acquiring, transferring or disposing of Securities, agreeing to do so, or procuring someone else to do so, whether on or off market.

rules.tier: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
rules.detail: Any monetisation structure that limits economic risk on vested Group Securities (collar, prepaid forward) is barred by para 9, and any secured financing is barred by para 16(a). An outright sale in a Trading Window with Pre-Clearance remains available.

CBA.exemption_authority: Group Chief Risk Officer is the Policy Exemption Authority. Trading Window exceptions are approved under Attachment A (CBA Board Chair for directors and the CEO; Board Audit Committee Chair for the Board Chair; CEO for Group Executives; Subsidiary Board Chair or Deputy Chair for subsidiary directors; Group General Counsel and Group Executive Legal & Group Secretariat for other Specified Persons and Board company secretaries). Any other exemption request goes through the Group Policy Framework.
jurisdiction_overlays: UK and EU Market Abuse Regulation No 596/2014: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and their Associates must not Trade any Group Security listed or traded on a UK or EU regulated market, or any other Security whose price or value depends on or affects such a Group Security (para 18).
Where laws, regulatory requirements or contractual obligations conflict with the policy, the more stringent standard applies.
ASB (New Zealand) has its own securities trading policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons and their Associates must not use Group Securities as security for margin lending or other secured financing arrangements, as a forced sale may lead to the breach of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly prohibited for every Specified Person, and there is no secured-lender-sale exception if the bank enforces.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Para 8 bans risk-limiting transactions on unvested or locked plan securities for all Specified Persons; para 9 extends the ban to any vested Group Securities only for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and their Associates.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedge leg is available only to Specified Persons outside the para 9 group (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors) and only over vested shares free of any holding lock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading involving conditional or limit orders (e.g. a specified, minimum sell or maximum purchase price or a stop-loss instruction) must be placed and executed during a Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar whose put or call is exercised or physically settled at maturity, or any price-triggered unwind, may execute outside a Trading Window and breach the policy unless cash-settled or timed to a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Off-market transfers with no change in beneficial ownership are exempt from Trading Windows other than those by the CBA Board directors and their Associates.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director transferring collared shares to a bank custodian or security account is making a Trade that must occur in a Trading Window with Pre-Clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Trading Window exception must be requested in writing with evidence that the proposed Trade is the most reasonable course of action and there are no other viable legal alternatives; it remains in force for seven calendar days unless revoked earlier, Pre-Clearance if required must be obtained within that period, Group Control Room must be notified, and confirmation of whether the Trade was placed must go to the approver and Group Control Room by the next business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hardship relief is drafted around a sale and does not extend to entering a hedge, so a collar cannot be executed in a closed period under it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and Associates must not Trade any other Security that has a price or value which depends on, or has an effect on, the price or value of a Group Security that is listed or traded on a UK or EU regulated market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's reference security or any Group Security it prices off is listed on a UK or EU market, the derivative is barred outright for this group regardless of Trading Windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition on Insider Trading applies at all times and overrides any Pre-Clearance, exception or other provision of this Policy. Pre-Clearance or an exception being granted is not an endorsement of any Trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pre-Clearance does not protect the executive or the bank if the executive holds Inside Information when the collar is struck.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If Group Securities make up 20% or more of an exchange traded fund (ETF) at the time of placing a Trade, the ETF is considered to be a Group Security for the purposes of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hedge referenced to a CBA-heavy ETF is treated as a hedge of Group Securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Specified Person list is not exhaustive and other individuals may be considered Specified Persons; designation is recorded on the Conflicts Hub and may change from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should confirm the counterparty's current designation and whether they fall in the para 9 group before structuring, since the answer differs between tiers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If Pre-Clearance requirements apply to you, you should refer to the Procedure for further information including how to seek Pre-Clearance and for which types of Trading it is required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Whether an OTC derivative specifically requires Pre-Clearance is settled by the unpublished Procedure, not this policy.

CBA.summary: A funded collar is not possible for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives or their Associates: para 9 bans any transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities, and para 16(a) bans using Group Securities as security for margin lending or any other secured financing. For other Specified Persons (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors, Group Control Room staff), the hedge leg over vested shares free of any holding lock is not expressly banned, but the OTC options are Securities and entering them is a Trade, so it must be done in a Trading Window, with Pre-Clearance where designated on the Conflicts Hub (valid three business days), subject to the 30-day LIFO holding rule, and it must not involve CFDs, short selling or stock lending of Group Securities. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited for all Specified Persons, so at most an unsecured or unfunded collar is workable for that group, and exercise or settlement mechanics that execute outside a Trading Window are a further risk under para 11. Employees who are not Specified Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and whatever Pre-Clearance the unpublished Procedure imposes. The MAR overlay in para 18 adds an outright bar for the senior group on any Security that prices off a UK/EU-listed Group Security.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on Derivatives (s761D, expressly including options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars) over unvested Group Securities for all NAB People. Vested means NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles satisfied, ignoring any longer restriction the person elected.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, all NAB People are prohibited from using Derivatives or otherwise entering into Hedging Arrangements in relation to any unvested Group Securities.

rules.detail: KMP (Directors and ELT) and their Closely Related Parties may not use Derivatives over remuneration elements that have vested but remain subject to forfeiture (clawback/malus) conditions.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Closely Related Parties must not use Derivatives or otherwise enter into Hedging Arrangements in relation to elements of their remuneration that are unvested or which have vested but remain subject to forfeiture conditions.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Group Securities are allowed only (a) to protect an asset supporting a loan for the exercise price of NAB options, (b) to protect value where a tax liability is payable at the tax cessation time, or (c) case-by-case with approval from the Chair (Directors), Group Company Secretary (Chair) or Group CEO or delegate (ELT and all other NAB People). Every Derivative must mature within the eight-week period immediately following release of half-year or full-year results, and no Group member may be counterparty. Directors and Designated NAB Employees must also lodge a Compliance Certificate. Venue is unrestricted, so an OTC collar with an external bank qualifies.
rules.evidence: once Group Securities have vested (as described above), Derivatives may be used by NAB People in relation to those vested securities in the following circumstances: ... on a case-by-case basis with approval from either the Chair in relation to Directors, the Group Company Secretary in relation to the Chair or the Group Chief Executive Officer or delegate in relation to Executive Leadership Team members and all other NAB People.

rules.detail: Hedging Arrangements (any arrangement limiting exposure to risk, including Corporations Regulation 2D.7.01(1) arrangements) over unvested Group Securities are banned for all NAB People; the policy notes it is also unlawful for KMP.
rules.evidence: all NAB People are prohibited from using Derivatives or otherwise entering into Hedging Arrangements in relation to any unvested Group Securities.

rules.evidence: Directors and Executive Leadership Team members (but not other Designated NAB Employees) must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan or agree to provide additional Group Securities as security for an existing Margin Loan.

rules.evidence: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative must have a maturity date that falls within the eight-week period that immediately follows the date on which either NAB's half-year or full-year financial results are released to the ASX
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's put and call must both expire within eight weeks after a results release, which fixes the available tenors (roughly six or twelve months from an open window) and rules out long-dated or open-ended structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: neither NAB nor any member of the Group can be a counterparty to the Derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and, prudently, the loan must be written by a bank outside the NAB Group; NAB's own markets desk cannot face the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives may be used by NAB People in relation to those vested securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by NAB; to protect the value of the Group Security where the employee has paid or is required to pay a tax liability at the tax cessation time; or on a case-by-case basis with approval
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A general funded collar falls outside the two self-executing purposes and needs discretionary case-by-case approval (Chair for Directors, Group Company Secretary for the Chair, Group CEO or delegate for ELT and others) in addition to the Compliance Certificate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Group Securities are considered vested once the NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a NAB Person has opted for a longer period of restriction
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares under a voluntary extended holding lock are collar-eligible, but for KMP shares that remain subject to forfeiture conditions after vesting are still off limits under 3.5.5.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank loan secured on the collared shares is a Margin Loan regardless of label, so Directors and ELT must lodge a Compliance Certificate before drawdown and before any collateral top-up.

bespoke_clauses.clause: NAB will publicly disclose all Derivative positions over Group Securities taken out by a Director or by Key Management Personnel of the Group ... irrespective of whether or not the particular form of Derivative technically falls within the disclosure requirements of the ASX Listing Rules or the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's or ELT member's collar will be announced to the market and reported in the Annual Financial Report even if it would not otherwise be notifiable, so confidentiality of the structure cannot be assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team are required to inform the Group Company Secretary where a financier demands payment under a Margin Loan and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any loan-to-value breach or margin call on the funded collar may have to be escalated internally and potentially disclosed to the market; the policy is silent on whether a forced sale in a Black-out Period is a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Acknowledgment of the Compliance Certificate by NAB is intended as a compliance monitoring function only, and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The certificate is a no-inside-information confirmation acknowledged by the Chair or manager rather than a substantive approval, and the Trade must occur within 5 business days of acknowledgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Performance rights must only be exercised outside the Black-out Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares to be collared must be settled from exercise outside the roughly six-week Black-out Periods beginning 16 March and 16 September, and the collar itself as a Trade in Derivatives is likewise confined to open periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Must not: Means an action is explicitly prohibited and any deviation from this will require a formal policy exemption.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Written exemptions are available only in Exceptional Circumstances (hardship or legal compulsion to sell), so they cannot be used to permit a collar over unvested or forfeitable securities.

NAB.summary: A funded collar is possible for NAB Directors and Executive Leadership Team members, but only over Group Securities whose NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied and, for KMP, that are no longer subject to forfeiture conditions; derivatives and hedging over unvested securities are banned outright. Because a general collar is not one of the two self-executing permitted purposes, it requires case-by-case approval (Chair for Directors, Group Company Secretary for the Chair, Group CEO or delegate for ELT), and both legs must mature within the eight-week period after a half-year or full-year results release and be written by a counterparty outside the NAB Group. The loan secured on the collared shares is a Margin Loan under the policy's broad definition, so Directors and ELT must lodge a Compliance Certificate before entering it and before any collateral top-up, and must report to the Group Company Secretary if a margin demand may force a sale. The derivative itself needs a Compliance Certificate, execution within 5 business days of acknowledgement, and must fall outside the 16 March and 16 September Black-out Periods and any ad hoc restriction; NAB will publicly disclose all Director and KMP derivative positions. Written exemptions exist only for hardship or court-ordered sales.

WBC.title: Westpac Group Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Directors of Westpac and its controlled entities, and all employees, secondees and contractors in Australia and overseas. Bound only by Section 3: insider trading ban, ban on derivatives/hedging over unvested Westpac securities, and the short-term trading ban. No blackout, notification or approval obligations unless also a Prescribed Employee.

tiers.name: Prescribed Employees
tiers.description: Umbrella term for Westpac Directors, Group Executives, Key Prescribed Employees and other employees on the Group Control Room's Register who are likely to have access to material financial, operational or strategic information. Subject to Section 4: Blackout Periods, ad hoc restrictions, the margin loan rules and the short selling ban. Those who are not Key Prescribed Employees or Directors trade on prior online notification to the Group Control Room.

tiers.name: Key Prescribed Employees
tiers.description: Prescribed Employees in senior positions whose trading may attract heightened regulatory or reputational scrutiny, listed on a separate register. Must pre-clear trades under the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process (an addendum not included in the lodged Policy) and disclose any margin lending arrangements to the Group Control Room.

tiers.name: Group Executives
tiers.description: Group Executives are Prescribed Employees; distinguished only for Blackout Period exemption applications (to the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive) and the 3Y notice follow-up.

tiers.name: Westpac Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Westpac Banking Corporation. Must obtain the Chairman's approval (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman) before buying or selling Westpac securities or entering a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities, and notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately after any trading.

tiers.name: associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, dependent children, trustees of trusts under which the person, spouse or dependent children may be beneficiaries, companies the person controls or holds a majority of, and any other entity of which the person is a director, secretary or executive officer, unless arrangements ensure the person takes no part in and did not procure the trading decision. Also called employee related accounts.

The Group Control Room notifies Prescribed Employees before Blackout Periods start and end; confidentiality of ad hoc restrictions is not addressed.

rules.detail: All Employees are barred from options, derivatives or other arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested Westpac securities or unvested employee share plan entitlements. No venue limit.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on hedging unvested Westpac securities and unvested employee share plan entitlements for all Employees.
rules.evidence: Use of derivatives and hedging over unvested Westpac securities is prohibited

rules.detail: Hedging vested Westpac securities is expressly permitted with prior Chairman approval and immediate post-trade notification to the General Manager, Company Secretary; associates' hedges are included.
rules.evidence: Westpac Directors must also notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading by either themselves or their associates in Westpac securities including entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities.

rules.detail: Prior online notification to the Group Control Room before entering a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities.
rules.evidence: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities; or arrange for another person to enter into arrangements of those kinds.

rules.detail: Hedging vested holdings is permitted subject to pre-clearance under the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process.
rules.evidence: Since Key Prescribed Employees must seek pre-clearance for trading in Westpac securities, they are not required to complete the online notification form

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or funded collar is an arrangement limiting economic risk, so it is banned over unvested holdings and over vested holdings follows the tier regime: Chairman approval for Directors, pre-clearance for Key Prescribed Employees, online notification for other Prescribed Employees. Any transfer of shares that changes ownership is itself a trade.
rules.evidence: Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy.

rules.detail: Outright ban for Westpac Directors and all Prescribed Employees (including Key Prescribed Employees and Group Executives).
rules.evidence: Short selling by Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees is prohibited and will be considered a breach of this Policy.

rules.detail: The short selling ban in 4.9 applies only to Directors and Prescribed Employees; other Employees are covered only by the general short-term/speculative trading ban.
Securities lending is not mentioned; lending shares would however be a change in ownership and so a trade for Prescribed Employees.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives and so securities, subject to the tier notification/approval regime; a CFD limiting risk on unvested holdings is banned, a short CFD offends the short selling ban and a speculative CFD the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: Short-term or speculative trading is prohibited and all employees must conduct their personal trading activities with a medium to long term perspective.

rules.detail: Margin loans over Westpac holdings are expressly permitted for Directors and Prescribed Employees, but margin calls cannot be met by selling Westpac securities during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information, a lender's sale in a Blackout Period is a breach regardless of instructions, and holders are expected to have other resources and to prefer facilities without price triggers. Entry into the loan itself needs no notification or approval except for Key Prescribed Employees' disclosure.
rules.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees are permitted to take out margin loans over their holdings in Westpac securities, however margin calls are not to be met by the sale of Westpac securities at a time when they would not be permitted to trade Westpac securities under this Policy.

rules.detail: Same permission and margin-call restrictions as other Prescribed Employees, plus mandatory disclosure of any margin lending arrangements over Westpac securities to the Group Control Room.
rules.evidence: In addition, Key Prescribed Employees are required to provide disclosure to the Group Control Room of any margin lending arrangements they may have in respect to Westpac securities.

rules.detail: Section 4.8 applies only to Directors and Prescribed Employees.

Granting security is not named as a trade; it is implicitly permitted because margin loans over Westpac holdings are allowed. A transfer of legal title to a lender or its nominee could be a change in ownership and so a trade requiring notification or approval.
rules.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees are permitted to take out margin loans over their holdings in Westpac securities

rules.detail: Only margin loans are named; a bank loan secured on Westpac shares with price triggers is functionally a margin loan and should be treated as within 4.8 (forced-sale restrictions, breach on lender sale in Blackout, disclosure by Key Prescribed Employees). The policy steers holders toward facilities without price triggers secured against other assets.
rules.evidence: they should take steps to rearrange their affairs to have a facility that does not contain price triggers (for example, an investment loan secured against other assets).

rules.detail: Short-term or speculative trading (entry to exit within a few days to a few weeks) is prohibited for all Employees; a loss-avoidance sale shortly after purchase should be raised with the Group Control Room.
rules.evidence: Short-term or speculative trading is prohibited and all employees must conduct their personal trading activities with a medium to long term perspective.

clearance.approver: Chairman (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_to: General Manager, Company Secretary (any trading by the Director or associates, including hedging arrangements over vested securities)

Section 4 contains specific obligations for Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees (including Group Executives and Key Prescribed Employees) ("Prescribed Employees") and applies only to them.

may participate in dividend reinvestment plans, rights issues or bonus issues ("corporate actions") which are offered to all Westpac shareholders, even where the corporate action is made, or acceptance falls, within a Blackout Period.

unless appropriate arrangements are in place to ensure you: take no part in the decision to purchase or sell securities (including Westpac securities); and have not procured or encouraged that other person, trust, company or any other entity to purchase or sell securities

financing_disclosure: Key Prescribed Employees: any margin lending arrangements in respect of Westpac securities (inception, ongoing); to the Group Control Room; deadline unspecified

Westpac Directors and Group Executives: where approval to sell during a Blackout Period is granted; advise the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive and General Manager, Company Secretary for any 3Y notice; before lodgement

WBC.exemption_authority: Blackout Period sale exemptions for unreasonable financial impost or other exceptional circumstances: Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive for Group Executives, Key Prescribed Employees and Prescribed Employees; Chairman for Westpac Directors; Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman. Written application confirming no inside information and that sale is the only reasonable course; written outcome with conditions; reasons may be withheld; the approver must decline if they themselves hold inside information. The Chief Compliance Officer may extend or reduce Blackout Periods. No general power to waive the unvested hedging ban or short selling ban.
jurisdiction_overlays: Employees working or dealing outside Australia must also comply with the laws of that jurisdiction; the Policy is based on Australian law

bespoke_clauses.clause: If your margin lender sells any of your Westpac securities during a Blackout Period, whether on your instructions to do so or not, it will be considered a breach of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement of the collared shares by the bank during the 15 March or 15 September Blackout Periods puts the Director or executive in breach even if involuntary, so the facility must not permit lender sales in those windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Westpac securities cannot be sold to meet a margin call during a Blackout Period or if you are in receipt of inside information relating to Westpac.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any loan-to-value shortfall on the funded collar must be met in cash or other assets during Blackout Periods or while the executive holds inside information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Westpac Director or Prescribed Employee has any doubt about their ability to meet a margin call by means other than a sale of their Westpac securities, they should take steps to rearrange their affairs to have a facility that does not contain price triggers (for example, an investment loan secured against other assets).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with a put floor can support a loan without price triggers, which aligns with the policy's stated preference, but a facility with LTV triggers requires demonstrable alternative resources.

bespoke_clauses.topic: change of ownership is a trade
bespoke_clauses.clause: Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy. This includes a transfer to a family member, family trust or personal superannuation scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving collared shares into a lender's nominee or a sponsored holding may itself be a trade needing notification or Chairman approval and must occur outside Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities; or arrange for another person to enter into arrangements of those kinds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar is expressly recognised as a permissible hedging arrangement over vested securities, subject to the tier's approval or notification and Blackout Periods, and the arranging limb catches hedges placed through associates or the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition, Key Prescribed Employees are subject to the requirements as set out in the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process, which is an Addendum to this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For senior executives the operative pre-clearance terms (approver, validity, conditions) sit in an unpublished addendum that must be obtained before structuring.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which you, your spouse or partner or your dependent children, is or may be a beneficiary; any company in which you hold (directly or indirectly) a majority of the shares or otherwise control
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan written to a family trust or controlled company is treated as the executive's own trade unless the executive is fully excluded from the decision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chief Compliance Officer has discretion to extend or reduce (conditionally or unconditionally) the Blackout Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Open windows are not fixed; collar entry, roll or unwind dates must be confirmed with the Group Control Room close to execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Westpac Directors must also notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading by either themselves or their associates in Westpac securities including entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar will be notified to the Company Secretary immediately and reported to ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A, so the structure will be public.

WBC.summary: A funded collar over vested Westpac shares is possible for Directors and Prescribed Employees. Derivatives and hedging over unvested holdings or unvested plan entitlements are prohibited for everyone, but hedging arrangements over vested securities are expressly contemplated: Directors need prior approval of the Chairman (Board Audit Committee Chairman for the Chairman) and must notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately afterwards; Key Prescribed Employees must pre-clear under the separate Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process; other Prescribed Employees lodge the online notification form beforehand; all must be outside the 15 March and 15 September Blackout Periods and any Chief Compliance Officer ad hoc restriction. Margin loans over Westpac securities are expressly permitted without approval (Key Prescribed Employees must disclose them to the Group Control Room), so the secured loan leg is available, but margin calls may not be met by selling Westpac shares in a Blackout Period or while holding inside information, any lender sale in a Blackout Period is a breach whether or not instructed, and the policy expects other resources and steers toward facilities without price triggers. Tenor should be medium to long term to avoid the short-term trading ban, and any transfer of the collared shares that changes ownership is itself a trade.

ANZ.title: Trading in ANZ Securities Policy

tiers.name: Employees, contingent workers and ANZ Directors
tiers.description: Everyone in the ANZ Group. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and the market perception test; the additional obligations (pre-trade approval, Blackout Periods, prohibited activities) apply only to ANZ Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: ANZ Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Employees likely to have access to material information, including ANZ Directors, ExCo Members, Key Management Personnel, all Group 1 and 2 staff and their executive assistants, the ANZ Control Room and anyone designated by a Risk Owner or ExCo Member. Must obtain Pre-trade Approval via the Personal Account Dealing Platform, observe Blackout Periods, and comply with the prohibited activities (speculative trading, short sales, margin/LTV financing, hedging unvested or locked plan holdings, 30-day minimum hold). Must treat Associates' transactions as their own.

tiers.name: ExCo Members and Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Group Executives reporting directly to the CEO, and KMP under GN27/AASB 124. Restricted Persons who must additionally obtain written Pre-trade Approval from the CFO, Chief Risk Officer or Group General Counsel via the platform and lodge a copy with the ANZGHL Company Secretary.

tiers.name: ANZ Directors and Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: Directors of ANZBGL, ANZGHL or a controlled entity (non-employees) and the CEO. Restricted Persons who must obtain written Pre-trade Approval from the Chairman of the ANZGHL Board (Chairman of the Audit Committee if unavailable) outside Blackout Periods and provide a copy to the Company Secretary. Directors of ANZGHL subsidiaries (other than ANZBGL) apply via the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, children under 18, dependants or anyone whose investment decisions the Restricted Person can reasonably be expected to influence or control, and any corporation, SMSF, partnership or trust over which the Restricted Person or their Associate has influence or control.

Confidentiality of the restriction is not addressed.

rules.detail: Options, derivatives or other hedging arrangements limiting economic risk of unvested incentive plan holdings are banned for Restricted Persons and Associates; no venue limit.

rules.evidence: or a holding subject to a holding lock or clawback period under an ANZ employee or executive incentive plan in ANZ Securities

rules.detail: Derivatives over unrestricted shares are not expressly addressed. An option or derivative relating to ANZ shares is itself an ANZ Security and any transaction affecting an interest in ANZ Securities is a Trade, so an OTC put/call requires Pre-trade Approval (Chairman for Directors/CEO; CFO, CRO or Group General Counsel for ExCo/KMP; platform for others), valid 48 hours, outside Blackout Periods, subject to the speculative trading ban, 30-day hold and market perception test.

rules.tier: Employees, contingent workers and ANZ Directors
rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and the market perception test; no derivative, hedging or financing restrictions are imposed on them.
rules.evidence: Additional requirements apply to ANZ Restricted Persons and their Associates to manage risk arising from the Trading in ANZ Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging unvested incentive plan holdings (ANZ Rights: deferred share rights, performance rights, restricted rights).

rules.evidence: any transaction or change affecting title to or interest in ANZ Securities or ANZ Rights

rules.detail: Outright ban for Restricted Persons and Associates.

Entering a CFD relating to ANZ Securities is expressly a Trade requiring Pre-trade Approval; in practice a CFD would fall foul of the speculative trading ban, the 30-day hold, the short sale ban (if short) and the margin/LTV financing ban, and a CFD over unvested or locked plan holdings is prohibited hedging.
rules.evidence: entering a contract for difference (CFD) relating to ANZ Securities,

bespoke_clauses.clause: not use ANZ Securities in connection with a margin loan or similar financing arrangements that may be subject to a margin call or loan to value ratio;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares with any LTV covenant or margin call right is prohibited outright for Directors, ExCo, KMP and all other Restricted Persons and their Associates; only a facility with no margin call or LTV mechanism falls outside the literal ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban extends to locked and clawback shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: an unvested holding or a holding subject to a holding lock or clawback period under an ANZ employee or executive incentive plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vested deferred or restricted shares cannot be collared until both the holding lock and any clawback period have expired; only unencumbered plan shares or on-market purchases are eligible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any transaction or change affecting title to or interest in ANZ Securities or ANZ Rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting a charge, transferring shares to a lender's nominee, and each put/call leg are all Trades requiring Pre-trade Approval outside Blackout Periods, and unwinds or settlements need fresh approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: outside of Blackout Periods, a transfer of ANZ Securities from a Broker Account held solely in the name of the ANZ Restricted Person and/ or Associate to another Broker Account held in the ANZ Restricted Person and/ or Associate's own name.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only same-name transfers are exempt from Pre-trade Approval; moving collared shares into a bank custody or nominee account is a Trade needing approval, and the August 2026 update was specifically made to tighten controls on off-market transfers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and contingent workers must not engage in Trading in ANZ Securities where the proposed Trade could be perceived as taking advantage of their position.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar can be refused or later criticised if it could be seen as exploiting the executive's position, giving approvers a broad discretionary veto.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Blackout Periods commence: Two months prior to the announcement of ANZ's half year and full year financial results; Two weeks prior to any periodic ANZ market trading updates
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Roughly five to six months of each year are closed, plus trading-update and ad hoc blackouts, so collar entry, rolls, resets and unwinds must be scheduled into narrow open windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Pre-trade Approvals are valid for 48 hours. Limit orders which have not been executed within 48 hours require a new Pre-trade Approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 48 hours of approval, and approval lapses if the executive receives Inside Information before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: ANZ Restricted Persons must treat their Associates' transactions for the purpose of this Policy and applicable laws as if the transactions were their own.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, SMSF, trust or controlled company does not avoid the financing ban or approval requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Acknowledgement of a Pre-trade Approval by or on behalf of ANZ is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval gives no comfort that the structure complies with insider trading law or the prohibited activities list; the executive bears that risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptions to this Policy will only be granted in exceptional circumstances. For example, where the ANZ Restricted Person is experiencing severe financial hardship or has an unanticipated significant financial commitment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A waiver of the margin/LTV financing ban for a routine funded collar is unlikely; the exception route is reserved for hardship and needs both Line Manager and Control Room approval.

ANZ.summary: A funded collar as typically structured is not available to ANZ Directors, ExCo Members, KMP or other Restricted Persons: section 3.5 prohibits using ANZ Securities in connection with a margin loan or any similar financing arrangement that may be subject to a margin call or loan-to-value ratio, and exceptions are granted only in exceptional circumstances such as severe hardship. The unfunded collar legs (put and call) over shares that are vested, outside any holding lock and past any clawback period are not prohibited, but each is a Trade requiring written Pre-trade Approval from the ANZGHL Chairman for Directors and the CEO, or from the CFO, Chief Risk Officer or Group General Counsel for ExCo and KMP, valid for 48 hours, outside the long Blackout Periods (two months before results, two weeks before trading updates, plus ad hoc periods), with a medium to long term objective, a 30-day minimum hold and the market perception test. Hedging unvested, locked or clawback-period plan holdings is banned outright. Any charge over the shares or transfer into a bank nominee account is itself a Trade needing approval, and a loan with no margin call or LTV mechanism, while outside the literal ban, would still need approval and could be refused on perception grounds.

MQG.title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Macquarie Staff
tiers.description: All Macquarie employees, agency workers, interns, secondees and contractors/consultants deemed subject by RMG Employee Compliance, together with Key Management Personnel and Associates. May deal in Macquarie securities only during a Staff Trading Window with PTA pre-clearance (or as an Excluded Dealing or under an exceptional-circumstances waiver); barred from short-term trading, uncovered short selling and hedging unvested or restricted securities.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel

Additionally subject to section 2.4: annual disclosure of financing arrangements over Macquarie securities, immediate notification to the Company Secretary of securities lent, mortgaged or charged to a financier and of margin demands, pre-clearance to liquidate for a margin call, and a bar on hedging below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.

tiers.name: Executive Directors

rules.detail: Options, warrants, futures and structured products providing exposure to MQG shares are Macquarie securities, so any derivative transaction is a dealing that must be pre-cleared through PTA and placed during a Staff Trading Window. rules.evidence: Structured products providing exposure to MQG shares, including but not limited to ETFs; Futures contracts, options and warrants over MQG shares

rules.detail: Absolute ban at any time on transactions designed or intended to hedge exposure to unvested Macquarie securities (including MEREP RSUs, DSUs and PSUs).
rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff are not permitted at any time to enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge their exposure to Macquarie securities which have not vested or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.

rules.detail: The ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.
rules.evidence: or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.

rules.detail: Hedging unrestricted Macquarie securities is expressly permitted subject to PTA pre-clearance, business group approval and the general personal dealing requirements (Staff Trading Window, no Inside Information, no short-term trading).
rules.evidence: They can however enter into a transaction intended to hedge unrestricted Macquarie securities subject to pre-clearance and other general personal dealing requirements (and, in respect of Key Management Personnel, subject to section 2.4 below).

rules.detail: KMP (and Executive Directors) may hedge unrestricted securities with pre-clearance, but not so as to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement; a collar over MSR shares is therefore excluded. rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.

rules.detail: Same MSR floor as KMP: hedging permitted with pre-clearance only over shares in excess of the minimum personal shareholding requirement.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or funded collar is a structured product providing exposure to MQG shares and a hedge, so it requires pre-clearance in a Staff Trading Window over unrestricted securities only; the financing leg is permitted under 2.2.2/2.4 with collateral-sufficiency and (for KMP) disclosure obligations, and the KMP/Executive Director MSR floor applies.
rules.evidence: Macquarie considers dealing to include, without limitation, securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly), including entering into an agreement to trade.

rules.detail: Uncovered short selling arrangements in any security including Macquarie securities are prohibited even during an open window; covered short sales are not expressly addressed but would be dealings requiring pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading and uncovered short selling arrangements in relation to any security, include a Macquarie security (even if the designated Staff Trading Window is open).

rules.detail: Securities lending is not prohibited or named as a dealing; the only reference is the KMP obligation to inform the Company Secretary immediately if Macquarie securities have been lent to a financier.

CFDs are not named but are structured products providing exposure to MQG shares, so are dealings requiring pre-clearance in a window; a CFD would in practice offend the short-term trading ban and, if short, the uncovered short selling ban, and cannot hedge unvested or restricted securities.
rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading and uncovered short selling arrangements in relation to any security

rules.detail: Margin loans over Macquarie securities are permitted without pre-clearance for entry, with an expectation of sufficient cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls even in an extreme sudden downturn. Any sale to meet a margin call is a dealing subject to pre-clearance and the window regime.
rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls including during a period of extreme sudden market downturn.

rules.detail: KMP may take margin loans but must disclose financing arrangements annually, inform the Company Secretary immediately when securities are lent, mortgaged or charged to a financier, when the financier is or is likely to become entitled to demand payment, and when a demand cannot be met without disposing of at least 1% of issued securities; liquidating to meet a margin call requires PTA pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: Liquidating a position to satisfy a margin call requires pre-clearance against Macquarie's PTA system. KMP must annually disclose their financing arrangements relating to their Macquarie securities to Macquarie.

rules.detail: Granting security over Macquarie securities is not a listed dealing and is implicitly permitted because financing arrangements over Macquarie securities are contemplated. A transfer of beneficial ownership to a lender would be a dealing requiring pre-clearance.

rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls

rules.detail: Permitted with annual disclosure to Macquarie and immediate Company Secretary notification at inception of any charge and on margin-demand events; pre-clearance needed before liquidating to meet a call.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel (KMP) who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls

rules.detail: Short-term trading in any security including Macquarie securities is prohibited even in an open window; no period is defined.
rules.evidence: Macquarie Staff are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading and uncovered short selling arrangements in relation to any security, include a Macquarie security (even if the designated Staff Trading Window is open).

MQG.exemption_authority: A specific written waiver from the prohibition on dealing outside a Staff Trading Window may be granted in exceptional circumstances (compulsion of law, severe financial hardship, or other circumstances deemed exceptional) by the ANZ Regional Head of Compliance, Global Head of Compliance or Head of Risk Management Group on a request to RMG Employee Compliance supported by a statutory declaration; granted at Macquarie's absolute discretion, subject to expiry, withdrawable, and refusal is final and confidential. Staff Trading Windows themselves are set at Macquarie's discretion. No waiver route is stated for the hedging bans or the MSR floor.
