bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar (which limits economic risk) can only be written over shares held in excess of the executive's minimum personal shareholding requirement, so the collarable parcel must be sized after deducting the MSR.

bespoke_clauses.clause: They can however enter into a transaction intended to hedge unrestricted Macquarie securities subject to pre-clearance and other general personal dealing requirements (and, in respect of Key Management Personnel, subject to section 2.4 below).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar legs are expressly permitted over vested, unlocked shares with PTA pre-clearance in a Staff Trading Window; MEREP shares under holding lock or dealing restriction remain ineligible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Macquarie Staff who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls including during a period of extreme sudden market downturn.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is contemplated and not prohibited, but the executive is expected to be able to meet margin calls from other resources rather than by selling Macquarie shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liquidating a position to satisfy a margin call requires pre-clearance against Macquarie's PTA system.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale outside a Staff Trading Window would require pre-clearance that is only available in a window or under an exceptional-circumstances waiver, so the facility must not rely on forced sales of the collared shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must inform the Company Secretary immediately if ... the member of KMP holds Macquarie securities that have been lent, mortgaged, or charged to a financier; circumstances have arisen in which the financier is entitled or likely to become entitled to exercise a right under the finance arrangements to demand payment; the member of KMP expects that the demand will not able to be satisfied without the disposal of securities representing at least 1% of the total number of issued securities of Macquarie.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Charging the collared shares to the bank triggers immediate notification to the Company Secretary (and likely ASX disclosure of the director's interest), and any LTV or event-of-default trigger must also be reported immediately.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to Macquarie's discretion, a period of up to five weeks following the release of Macquarie's interim results (November/December), final results (May/June) and Annual General Meeting (July/August)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, any roll or reset, and unwind must each fall within one of three short discretionary windows a year, and the window may be shortened or withheld.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All pre-clearances are subject to an expiry date and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. A denied pre-clearance is final and binding on the Macquarie Staff member who made the request and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should expect that a cleared collar can be blocked before execution and that a refusal cannot be explained to it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Macquarie considers dealing to include, without limitation, securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly), including entering into an agreement to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Signing the collar confirmation or any agreement to deliver shares is a dealing at signing, and any transfer of beneficial ownership to a lender or nominee is separately a dealing requiring pre-clearance in a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Macquarie securities Includes, but is not limited to: ... Structured products providing exposure to MQG shares, including but not limited to ETFs; Futures contracts, options and warrants over MQG shares
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar with a bank is a structured product providing exposure to MQG shares and is caught with no venue limitation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A waiver request must be submitted to RMG Employee Compliance in writing, accompanied by a statutory declaration from the requesting Macquarie Staff member declaring that: the proposed dealing is the only reasonable action available; they do not possess non-public price-sensitive information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Out-of-window settlement, unwind or forced sale of the collared shares is available only through a hardship-style waiver at Macquarie's absolute discretion, which cannot be assumed in facility documentation.

MQG.summary: A funded collar is possible for Macquarie Staff including Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors, over Macquarie securities that have vested and are free of any holding lock or dealing restriction. The collar is a transaction intended to hedge unrestricted securities and is expressly permitted subject to PTA pre-clearance and business group approval, executed within a discretionary Staff Trading Window of up to five weeks after the interim results, final results or AGM; hedging unvested or locked securities (including MEREP awards) is banned at any time, and KMP and Executive Directors cannot hedge below their minimum personal shareholding requirement. Margin loans and other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities are permitted, with an expectation of sufficient cash or other collateral to meet margin calls even in an extreme downturn; KMP must disclose financing arrangements annually, inform the Company Secretary immediately when shares are lent, mortgaged or charged to a financier and on any margin-demand event or anticipated disposal of 1% or more of issued securities, and any liquidation to meet a margin call needs pre-clearance, which is available only in a window or under an exceptional-circumstances waiver. Short-term trading and uncovered short selling are prohibited, so the collar should be medium term and physically settled only in a window.

WES.title: Securities Trading Policy (Policy No: 1.4)

tiers.name: All directors and employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of the Wesfarmers Group. Subject only to the insider trading prohibitions (dealing, tipping, applying to a share plan while holding inside information) and any Project Restrictions; no clearance, blackout, hedging or financing restrictions apply at this level.

tiers.name: Officers
tiers.description: Directors of Wesfarmers and members of the Wesfarmers Leadership Team. Subject to Annexure B: prior clearance from the Company Secretary for every dealing in Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities, Blackout Periods, and clearance-gated restrictions on short-term dealing, short selling, security interests, margin loans and hedging.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Wesfarmers; an Officer subset distinguished by Chairman (or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) sign-off on clearance, a wider Associated Party net (any person or entity whose dealing would require ASX disclosure by the director), Corporations Act and Listing Rule notification obligations, a Board Charter minimum shareholding and a letter agreement on notification of trading.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family members living with an Officer (or whose investment decisions the Officer controls), any company, trust, managed superannuation fund or other entity controlled by the Officer or such family member, and, for directors only, any person or entity whose dealing would require ASX disclosure by the director (including where the director controls voting or disposal or is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver Wesfarmers securities).

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of that director or senior executive to risk relating to an element of that director or senior executive's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal

WES.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: 'Project Restrictions' may be imposed from time to time on nominated directors and employees due to their knowledge of a potential project or transaction. The policy does not say who imposes them or whether they are confidential; the Company Secretary's clearance confirmation covers whether the dealing is 'subject to any other restriction under this policy'.

rules.detail: Derivative trading is not named as a restricted activity, but 'securities' expressly includes equity swaps, CFDs, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, and dealing includes creating a hedge or other financial interest over or in relation to securities. An OTC put or call with a bank is therefore a dealing requiring the full Annexure B 3 clearance process and is barred in Blackout Periods. For an off-market dealing the dealing occurs at settlement, which must fall within two clear trading days of clearance.
rules.evidence: securities includes shares, options, notes, bonds and other debentures, interests in managed investment schemes, trusts and other financial products, and any derivatives of those securities, including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Employees who are not Officers may deal in derivatives over Wesfarmers securities subject only to not holding inside information and any Project Restrictions; no clearance or blackout applies.
rules.evidence: All directors and employees of the Wesfarmers Group are prohibited from: (a) dealing in any securities where the person dealing in the securities has inside information in relation to those securities

rules.detail: The policy restates the Corporations Act prohibition on KMP and their closely related parties limiting exposure to risk relating to remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal, and states that clearance cannot be obtained for such dealings. Applies to Officers who are KMP.
rules.evidence: Clearance cannot be obtained from the Wesfarmers Company Secretary under paragraph 3 of this Annexure B for dealings which are restricted by the Corporations Act.

rules.detail: The Corporations Act restriction as restated applies to any element of remuneration that 'remains subject to restrictions on disposal', which captures vested shares still under a holding lock or disposal restriction under a share plan. No clearance is available.
rules.evidence: from entering into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of that director or senior executive to risk relating to an element of that director or senior executive's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal.

rules.detail: Hedging Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities is prohibited for Officers and Associated Parties unless approval is sought and clearance obtained from the Company Secretary and all Annexure B 3 steps are complied with. Clearance is discretionary and will not be given where the 'front page' test is failed.
rules.evidence: Each Officer and their Associated Parties are prohibited from engaging in the following dealings: ... (e) hedging Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities, unless approval has been sought and clearance obtained from the Wesfarmers Company Secretary, and all steps outlined in paragraph 3 of this Annexure B have been complied with.

rules.detail: Creating a hedge is a dealing, but for non-Officer employees the only constraints are the insider trading prohibition, Project Restrictions and share plan rules. Non-KMP employees are outside the Corporations Act hedging restriction restated in Annexure B 9.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A prepaid forward, funded collar or similar is a dealing (agreeing to sell; creating a financial interest over securities) requiring clearance, and any secured or financial interest component falls within the express Annexure B 9(d) clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: any other transfer or creation of an interest in securities, whether directly, or by arranging for someone else to undertake the dealing on your behalf; and (vii) agreeing or applying to do any of the above.

rules.detail: Short selling by Officers and Associated Parties is prohibited unless approval is sought and clearance obtained from the Company Secretary; it is not an absolute ban.
rules.evidence: (c) entering into instruments or transactions to borrow and sell Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities with the intention of buying Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities back at a later date (short selling)

rules.detail: The short selling restriction is confined to Annexure B (Officers); the general policy is silent for other employees.

Lending securities is not named. Transferring legal ownership even where beneficial ownership does not change is a dealing, so lending shares to a bank (or delivering them to a custodian) requires Officer clearance. Borrowing to sell is caught as short selling under Annexure B 9(c).
rules.evidence: transferring legal ownership of securities, even where beneficial ownership does not change

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are named in the definition of securities, so dealing in a CFD over Wesfarmers securities requires clearance; a short CFD would also fall within the short selling and short-term dealing restrictions of Annexure B 9.

Entering into a margin loan is also a dealing under Annexure A 1(a)(iv).
rules.evidence: (d) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan in respect of, Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities

Creating a security interest is also itself a dealing, so it attracts Blackout Periods and, for off-market dealings, the settle-within-two-trading-days rule.
rules.evidence: (d) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan in respect of, Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities

WES.exemption_authority: Wesfarmers Company Secretary grants or refuses clearance at discretion without reasons, after confirming with at least two disclosure committee members (and the Chairman, or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, for directors). Blackout Period relief is limited to sales in exceptional circumstances with the Chairman's (or ARC Chair's) prior written approval and documentary evidence. The CFO may approve share plan issues to Project-Restricted employees. No clearance can be given for dealings restricted by the Corporations Act. Only the Board may amend the policy.
jurisdiction_overlays: Corporations Act restriction on KMP and closely related parties hedging remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal; clearance cannot be given for such dealings

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of an on-market trade, the dealing occurs at execution (but not settlement) of the trade. In the case of an off-market trade, the dealing occurs at settlement of the trade. ... in the case of an off-market dealing, settle the dealing, in Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities within two clear trading days of receiving confirmation from the Wesfarmers Company Secretary
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar and secured loan are off-market dealings, so signing, funding and security grant must all settle within two clear trading days of clearance and outside a Blackout Period, which drives the execution timetable with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval under this Policy is required for a dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a policy-compliant collar can be refused if the Company Secretary considers the market would perceive it as an inappropriate use of position, so reputational optics of hedging director exposure are a live gating factor.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Corporations Act restricts directors and senior executives of the Wesfarmers Group who are classified as 'key management personnel' ... from entering into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of that director or senior executive to risk relating to an element of that director or senior executive's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal. Clearance cannot be obtained ... for dealings which are restricted by the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar may only be written over shares that are both vested and free of any plan disposal restriction; vested shares still subject to a holding lock cannot be collared by KMP and no waiver is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Wesfarmers Company Secretary, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Wesfarmers Company Secretary at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should not price or commit until clearance is in hand, and the transaction can be pulled up to the moment of settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The only exception to the prohibition on dealing during Blackout Periods is a sale of Wesfarmers securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, rolling, restriking or granting security under a collar can never occur in a Blackout Period; only a hardship or court-ordered sale, or a no-change-of-beneficial-ownership transfer, can be approved inside a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in relation to Wesfarmers directors only, any other person or entity where dealing in Wesfarmers securities by that person or entity would require disclosure to the ASX by the Wesfarmers director. This includes where the Wesfarmers director: (i) controls the right to vote or dispose of Wesfarmers securities; or (ii) is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for, or deliver Wesfarmers securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a trust, company or superannuation fund does not avoid clearance, and the option contracts themselves are the type of interest that brings a vehicle into the director's Associated Party net.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees who acquire Wesfarmers securities under a Wesfarmers share plan must also comply with the rules of that plan when dealing in those securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Plan rules (not in the policy) may impose holding locks or hedging bans over vested plan shares that would independently block a collar or security grant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional restrictions in this Annexure B apply to dealings in Wesfarmers and BWP Trust securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance regime and Annexure B 9 restrictions extend to BWP Trust units, although the Blackout Periods are expressed to apply only to Wesfarmers securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this does not include disposals of Wesfarmers securities within a short period of time after vesting or issuance of those securities under a share plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Newly vested shares can be sold or delivered under a collar without offending the three-month short-term rule, so the collar tenor need not be driven by the vesting date.

WES.summary: A funded collar is possible for Wesfarmers directors and Leadership Team members (Officers), but only with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, who must first confirm with at least two disclosure committee members and, for directors, the Chairman (or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee). Hedging, creating a security interest, entering a margin loan and any OTC derivative are each clearance-gated dealings under Annexure B 9 rather than prohibited, and the clearance is discretionary, revocable, subject to the 'front page' test and valid only for two clear trading days within which an off-market dealing must settle. The collar cannot be written over unvested shares or vested shares still subject to disposal restrictions because the policy restates the Corporations Act KMP hedging restriction and states that clearance cannot be given for it; only vested, unrestricted shares qualify, and plan rules must also be satisfied. Entry, security grant, roll and unwind must all fall outside the 20 June and 20 December Blackout Periods and any Project Restriction, since blackout relief is limited to sales in hardship or court-ordered circumstances. Lender enforcement and margin-call sales are not addressed, and directors must also comply with the Board Charter minimum shareholding and their ASX and letter-agreement notification obligations.

CSL.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Directors, members of the Global Leadership Group and their Related Parties are absolutely prohibited from entering hedging arrangements in relation to CSL Securities, which captures the put and call legs of a collar regardless of vesting state, and no approver can waive it. Separately, section 2.6 bans all Personnel from margin loans and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of CSL Securities, so the loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited for everyone. Personnel below the Global Leadership Group may enter an unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares only if it is initiated in an Open Period with its exercise date fixed within an Open Period, they hold no inside information and, if they are Restricted Persons, they obtain prior approval (Company Secretary or delegate) and deal within three ASX trading days. Key terms including Restricted Persons and Related Parties are undefined in the lodged document and must be confirmed with CSL.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited from undertaking any of the following Dealings with respect to Rio Tinto Securities: (a) Dealing in derivative products issued over or in respect of Rio Tinto Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both option legs of a collar are derivative products over Rio Tinto Securities, so no collar of any kind is available to directors, KMP or designated PDMRs, funded or not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (d) entering into margin lending or other secure financing arrangements in respect of Rio Tinto Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited for PDMRs with no exemption authority.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following types of Dealings are excluded from the operation of this Policy and may be undertaken by Restricted Persons at any time, without prior written clearance ... (f) a disposal of Rio Tinto Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For non-PDMR Restricted Persons who lawfully grant security, the bank's enforcement sale is outside the Policy even in a Closed Period, though the Insider Dealing prohibition still applies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (e) entering into a transaction the economic outcome of which is dependent upon the price of a Rio Tinto Security, including but not limited to a transaction which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of holding a Rio Tinto Security
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar with a bank is a Dealing regardless of venue or settlement method, so non-PDMR Permanent and Project Restricted Persons need prior written clearance for it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: charge under derivative contract is dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: (h) entering into any margin lending, derivative contract or other secured financial arrangement pursuant to which a charge is granted over the Rio Tinto Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security package of a funded collar is itself a Dealing, so the loan and charge must be cleared and executed inside the clearance window, not only the options.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Rio Tinto prohibits Permanent Restricted Persons, from entering into arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share ... (or a vested share ... that is still subject to disposal restrictions).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For non-PDMR Permanent Restricted Persons, only vested plan shares free of disposal restrictions, or non-plan shares, may be collared.

bespoke_clauses.clause: must Deal in Rio Tinto Securities within the period specified in the written clearance to Deal, or in the absence of a period being specified, within two Business Days of the receipt of the clearance to Deal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The approver can grant a longer execution window, which may be needed to document an OTC collar and security, but the default is two Business Days (UK and Australian holidays both excluded).

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company, trust, partnership or entity: which is managed by the PDMR or a family member; which is directly or indirectly controlled by the PDMR or a family member; which is set up for the benefit of the PDMR or a family member; or the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to the PDMR's or a family member's.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan taken through a family trust or private company is a PCA Dealing needing clearance and immediate notification, and the PDMR bans on derivatives and secured financing apply to Dealing 'for the account of a third party, directly or indirectly'.

bespoke_clauses.topic: post trade notification even if no deal
bespoke_clauses.clause: After receiving the clearance to deal, if Restricted Persons decide not to deal in Rio Tinto Securities, you still need to submit a Post Trading Notification promptly, indicating that you did not deal
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared but unexecuted collar still requires a portal notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial difficulty or compulsion by court order exist, which require an immediate sale of Rio Tinto Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closed Period relief is confined to immediate sales, so collar entry, roll or unwind cannot be cleared inside a Closed Period.

RIO.summary: A funded collar is not possible for Rio Tinto directors, KMP or any other PDMR: section 12.3 expressly prohibits PDMRs from Dealing in derivative products over or in respect of Rio Tinto Securities and from entering margin lending or other secured financing arrangements, with no exemption authority, and PCAs are caught through the 'for the account of a third party' language. For Permanent or Project Restricted Persons who are not PDMRs, a collar and a secured loan are each Dealings (limbs (c), (e) and (h) of the definition) that may proceed only with prior written clearance from the Group Company Secretary or delegate via the Dealing Rules portal, executed within two Business Days or the period specified, outside any Closed Period applying to them, with a Post Trade Notification within two business days. Such persons may not hedge unvested plan securities or vested plan securities still subject to disposal restrictions, so only vested, unrestricted or non-plan shares can be collared. A disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the Policy. Personnel who are not Restricted Persons are subject only to the Insider Dealing prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to the insider trading prohibitions outlined above, and other than in relation to dealings by Directors in black-out periods, the following dealings by a director or restricted employee are excluded from the operation of this Policy: ... disposal of Woodside securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A secured lender's enforcement sale is outside the Policy for restricted employees, but for a director it would be a black-out period breach; the same carve-back applies to custodian or depositary transfers by directors in black-out.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging vested holdings by restricted employees
bespoke_clauses.clause: These requirements also apply to dealings in financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Woodside securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly contemplates restricted employees outside the section 5 tier hedging vested holdings with a bank product, on Compliance Certificate acknowledgement by the Group General Counsel within a 7-day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Woodside will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Restructuring a collar as a cash-settled swap, a funded forward or a family-trust transaction will be judged by economic effect against the derivatives, hedging and pledging bans.

bespoke_clauses.topic: arrangements forcing disposal within three months
bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where financing is allowed, a loan or collar whose default or physical settlement could force delivery of shares acquired within the last three months is itself prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A response would normally be expected within 24 hours ... Any such approval will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Where a dealing is permitted, execution and settlement of documentation must fit in a 7-day window from approval or acknowledgement, and the approval can be conditioned or revoked before dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If any clearance, approval or acknowledgment is required for a dealing under this Policy, the clearance, approval or acknowledgement will not be granted if the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hedge or financing by a senior person can be refused on perception grounds alone, without reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy extends to all securities owned or controlled by a person covered by the Policy, whether those securities are held in the name of that person, in a company, through a trust, by a family member, by a friend or in some other entity or arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Placing the collared shares in a trust, company or nominee does not take the collar or pledge outside the bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Debt transactions that may be converted into Woodside shares are also prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A financing structured as an exchangeable or convertible instrument over Woodside shares is caught for the section 5 tier.

WDS.summary: A funded collar is not possible for Woodside directors, executive key management personnel or other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan: section 5.1 expressly prohibits transactions in Woodside-based derivative securities including collars and writing puts or calls, whether for hedging or not and regardless of vesting state, and section 8.1 separately bans directors, Company Secretaries and CEO direct reports from pledging Woodside securities as collateral, with no exemption authority. The only potential candidates are restricted employees nominated by the Group General Counsel who are not executive incentive plan participants or CEO direct reports: for them an OTC hedge of a vested, unlocked holding and a secured loan are each dealings requiring a Compliance Certificate acknowledged by the GGC, executed within 7 days, outside the 31 December and 30 June black-out periods, passing the Front Page Test and not forcing disposal of shares acquired within three months. Ordinary employees may enter such arrangements without notification subject to the insider trading, Front Page Test and short-term dealing rules. A secured lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the Policy except for directors in a black-out period, and all approvals are discretionary, conditionable and revocable.

rules.section: 1; 3; Derivatives and hedging over vested Goodman securities
rules.detail: Entering into a derivative contract is named as a Dealing and Securities include related financial products including options and derivatives with no venue limit, so an OTC put or call with a bank requires prior consent (Group CEO or Company Secretary; Chairman for Directors) valid for 10 business days and cannot be entered in a blackout period. Hedging derivatives carry the additional exercise-window condition below.

rules.section: Derivatives and hedging over vested Goodman securities
rules.detail: Derivative hedges of vested Goodman Securities are expressly permitted provided the exercise window for either party does not fall in a scheduled blackout period, the arrangement complies with the law, the rest of the policy (including consent) and any other conditions such as a minimum holding requirement. If an unscheduled blackout overlaps the exercise period, the derivative must not be exercised or settled and the Company Secretary must be informed.

rules.section: Derivatives and hedging over vested Goodman securities

rules.section: Use of derivatives and hedging over unvested Goodman securities is prohibited
rules.detail: Absolute ban on derivative contracts hedging exposure to unvested employee equity incentive plan securities, for all team members.
rules.evidence: It is contrary to this policy for team members to enter into derivative contracts that hedge their exposure to movements in the price of Securities provided under an employee equity incentive plan that have not vested.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or funded collar is a derivative contract (a Dealing needing consent) and, where secured on Goodman Securities, a loan subject to the margin lending rules; for key management personnel any structure characterised as a margin loan is banned.
rules.evidence: Deal in Securities (including trading, entering into a margin loan or derivative contract)

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling, defined as selling financial products not owned or borrowed with a view to repurchasing at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Short selling of Securities by team members is prohibited.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named; borrowing appears only within the definition of short selling.

rules.section: What are Goodman Securities?; 3; No short selling of Securities
rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are derivatives and so Securities; entering one is a Dealing requiring consent, a short CFD would offend the short selling ban and frequent CFD trading the short-term discouragement.

rules.detail: Entering a margin loan is a Dealing requiring consent. A margin call must not be met by selling Goodman Securities when trading is not allowed, the borrower must have other resources to meet calls, and a lender's sale during a prohibited time is a breach to be disclosed immediately to the Company Secretary for Board consideration.

rules.detail: KMP named in the most recent Remuneration Report (which includes directors) must not have any margin loan in respect of Goodman Securities; 'margin loan' is not defined and no approval route exists.
rules.evidence: Key management personnel (as defined in the Corporations Act and included in the most recent Remuneration Report) must not have a margin loan in respect of Goodman Securities.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or security interest is not named as a Dealing; the policy addresses security over Goodman Securities only in the context of margin loans.

Secured financing generally is not named; the margin lending section regulates a 'loan to acquire securities that is secured by Goodman Securities', and entering a margin loan is a Dealing needing consent. Other loans secured on Goodman Securities are not expressly addressed but would sensibly be treated the same way, with the forced-sale-in-blackout breach rule applying.

rules.detail: Only 'margin loan' is banned for KMP. Because the term is undefined and the policy elsewhere describes a margin loan as a loan secured by Goodman Securities, a bank loan secured on collared securities is likely to be characterised as a margin loan and so prohibited for KMP.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A team member can only enter into a derivative contract that hedges their exposure to movements in the price of Securities if the exercise window for either party under that contract is not during a scheduled blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's expiry, exercise and settlement dates for both the executive and the bank must be scheduled outside the 30 June, 31 December and quarterly-update blackouts, which rules out American-style or early-termination rights exercisable in those windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where an unscheduled blackout period overlaps with an exercise period, a team member must not seek to exercise or settle the derivative and should inform the Company Secretary. A Committee of the Chairman, Group CEO and the Company Secretary will consider appropriate actions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar documentation needs a mechanism to defer exercise or settlement if an ad hoc blackout is declared, since the executive cannot settle and the outcome depends on a Committee decision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are required to have sufficient resources to meet a margin call by means other than by a sale of your Goodman Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any loan secured on the collared shares must be structured so that top-ups can be met in cash, since selling the shares to meet a call when trading is not allowed is a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If your margin lender sells any of your Securities at a time when trading is not allowed, it will be considered a breach of this policy. Any dealing in breach of this policy should immediately be disclosed to the Company Secretary for reporting to and consideration by the Board for possible disciplinary action.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Bank enforcement rights over the collateral must be contractually suspended during blackouts and while the executive holds inside information, or the executive is exposed to disciplinary action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key management personnel (as defined in the Corporations Act and included in the most recent Remuneration Report) must not have a margin loan in respect of Goodman Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Margin loan' is undefined; a bank loan secured on collared securities with a top-up mechanism is likely to be treated as one, so the funded leg is unavailable to directors and Remuneration Report KMP even though the derivative legs are permitted with consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not trade the Securities until consent has been granted. Consent lasts 10 business days after which time you must again seek consent to trade. Consent may be withdrawn at any time before you trade in Securities if new relevant information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into the collar and the loan must complete within 10 business days of consent, and consent can be withdrawn before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The arrangement must also comply with the law, the other provisions of this policy and any other conditions that you may be subject to (such as a minimum holding requirement).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares subject to a minimum holding requirement may not be available to collar or deliver, and the bank should confirm whether hedged securities count towards that requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Special risks may arise where you do not have control of securities that may be acquired or sold in respect of which you have a beneficial interest. Care should be taken in relation to giving discretionary mandates where you have a direct or indirect interest in the securities, margin loans and derivatives
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Bank discretion to sell, rehypothecate or deliver collateral is flagged as a policy risk the executive bears.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Their associates which include close family members and people or entities (such as family companies or self managed pension funds) where there is any influence over the investment process or where they are acting on behalf of the Director or employee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family company or SMSF does not avoid consent, blackouts or the KMP margin loan ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent is also not required where trading in Securities results in no change to the beneficial interest in the Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving shares to the bank's custodian or nominee without change of beneficial interest needs no consent, though such 'trading' is not expressly excluded from blackout periods.

GMG.summary: For Goodman team members who are not key management personnel, a funded collar is possible: the policy expressly permits derivative contracts hedging vested Goodman Securities with prior consent from the Group CEO or Company Secretary (Chairman for Directors, Audit Committee Chair for the Chairman) valid for 10 business days, provided the exercise window for either party falls outside the scheduled 30 June, 31 December and quarterly-update blackouts, the arrangement respects any minimum holding requirement, and the collared securities are not unvested plan securities. A loan secured on Goodman Securities is permitted for such persons as a consented Dealing, but the executive must be able to meet margin calls from other resources, must not sell during a blackout to meet a call, and a lender's sale while trading is prohibited is a breach reportable to the Board. For directors and other KMP named in the Remuneration Report, the ban on having a margin loan in respect of Goodman Securities, with 'margin loan' undefined, makes the funded leg unavailable in practice, leaving only an unfunded collar with consent. Exercise or settlement during an unscheduled blackout is barred and referred to a Committee of the Chairman, Group CEO and Company Secretary.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule for vested, unlocked shares. Company Securities include derivatives and other financial products created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, and dealing includes buying or selling them or agreeing to do so, and any transaction limiting economic risk of a holding. An OTC put and call with a bank is therefore a dealing requiring prior Notification, execution within 7 days, and is barred during Prohibited Periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures, options or other securities able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange

rules.detail: Acquiring derivatives or options in relation to Company Securities that hedge or transfer the risk of fluctuation in value of an unvested entitlement (including equity rights subject to time and/or performance hurdles) is expressly banned.

rules.detail: The same express ban on acquiring derivatives or options extends to Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock. This would include acquiring derivatives or options in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions having the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of fluctuation in value of any unvested entitlement, including equity rights subject to time and/or performance hurdles. No approval route.

FMG.exemption_authority: Chairman (or, for the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit Committee) may give written clearance for a Designated Person not holding inside information to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period on demonstrated severe financial hardship, legal requirement to transfer, or other exceptional circumstances; the trade must occur within 7 days. No authority to waive the hedging, short-term dealing or short-selling bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not enter into transactions which would have the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of any fluctuation in the value of ... Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collared shares must be both vested and free of any plan holding lock; the bank should verify the lock status of each parcel before inception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: To deal and dealing includes ... entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar is a dealing in its own right regardless of venue or whether the OTC options are 'Company Securities', so Notification, the 7-day execution window and Prohibited Periods apply to inception, roll and unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures, options or other securities able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'able to be traded on ASX' qualifier could be read as limiting derivatives to exchange-traded products, but the economic-risk limb of dealing captures an OTC collar in any event.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notification means a notification in writing (including by email) that includes ... a confirmation that the Designated Person is not in possession of price sensitive information about the Company that is not generally available to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods no one approves the dealing; the executive self-certifies and must execute within seven days of the Notification, so the collar must be priced and signed inside that window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Season means each of: (a) the period from the end of the financial year or half financial year to the business day after the time of release of the annual or half year results; and (b) the period from the end of the September quarter or March quarter to the business day after the time of release of the September or March quarterly reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly reporting produces four closed seasons per year plus Board blackouts, narrowing the windows for inception, roll, unwind and physical settlement of the collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibited period relief is disposal only
bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Buying back the written call or purchasing a put to unwind or restructure during a Prohibited Period cannot be cleared even in hardship; only a disposal (e.g. delivery of shares on call exercise) could be.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must refrain from dealing in Company Securities during Prohibited Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale or for physical settlement at expiry, so a bank enforcing its security or exercising the call in a Closed Season could put the Designated Person in breach; expiry dates and enforcement mechanics should avoid Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short Term Dealing includes dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under three months, or an unwind within three months of inception, risks characterisation as Short Term Dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Designated Person may not deal in Company Securities, he or she must take all reasonable and necessary steps to prevent any dealing in Company Securities by Related Parties unless the Designated Person has complied with this Policy on behalf of that Related Party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company requires the Designated Person to make the Notification on the Related Party's behalf and observe Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A director is required to notify the Company Secretary if there is any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company ... with sufficient notice to allow the Company Secretary to make the necessary notifications within 5 business days after the change occurs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the security granted to the bank will be disclosed to ASX via Appendix 3Y, so the arrangement will be public within five business days.

FMG.summary: A funded collar over vested, unlocked shares is possible for Fortescue directors and executives under this policy. The put and call are a dealing (via the economic-risk limb of the dealing definition and the inclusion of third-party derivatives in Company Securities) and so require a prior written Notification (to the Chair of the Audit Committee and Company Secretary for the Chairman, the Chairman and Company Secretary for other directors, and the Company Secretary for other Designated Persons), execution within seven days, and must fall outside the four Closed Seasons and any Board blackout and not while holding inside information. Hedging of unvested entitlements and of vested shares still subject to a holding lock is absolutely prohibited. The loan and the security over the collared shares are not addressed at all: there is no margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing restriction and no disclosure requirement, but equally no forced-sale carve-out, and Prohibited Period clearance is discretionary and disposal-only, so settlement, enforcement and unwind mechanics should be timed to avoid Prohibited Periods and the collar tenor should exceed three months to avoid the Short Term Dealing ban.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not regulated as such. Securities expressly include warrants and other derivative products relating to Telstra securities whether created by Telstra or third parties (no venue limit), so a derivative is a dealing requiring window-period approval or notification. Any derivative that limits the economic risk of holding Telstra securities (a purchased put, a collar) is caught by the general hedging prohibition and is banned outright; forward contracts are deemed speculative short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: It also extends to financial products relating to securities issued by Telstra (for example, warrants and other derivative products) whether or not the financial products are created by Telstra or by third parties.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to paragraph 21, if you're a Designated Person, you are prohibited from entering into any hedging arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Telstra securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar (purchased put plus written call) is itself a hedging arrangement over vested shares and is banned for every director, executive KMP and their Closely Related Parties regardless of vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.clause: using Telstra securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including entering margin loan arrangements in respect of Telstra securities or transferring Telstra securities to an existing margin loan account
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited for Designated Persons, so both halves of a funded collar fail.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Despite paragraph 16, if you entered an arrangement prior to becoming a Designated Person that would otherwise be prohibited under paragraphs 16 b)-d), you are permitted to continue that arrangement for 12 months from the date that you became a Designated Person or until the date of expiry of the relevant arrangement, whichever occurs earlier.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar loan put in place before appointment as a Designated Person can run for at most 12 months after appointment; the hedge leg has a separate, Company Secretary-approved 'limited period' under paragraph 21.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you have any hedging arrangements in effect prior to becoming a Designated Person that would otherwise be prohibited under paragraph 19, you may, in certain limited circumstances with the approval of the Telstra Company Secretary, be permitted to continue such arrangements for a limited period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Continuation of an existing collar after appointment is discretionary and time-limited, so the bank cannot assume the hedge survives the client becoming a Designated Person.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Telstra securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights pursuant to an arrangement that was permitted under paragraph 17
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is an excluded dealing only for grandfathered pre-appointment arrangements; there is no carve-out for any other enforcement sale, and directors must notify the Company Secretary before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances, you may be granted approval to deal in Telstra securities in a way that's prohibited under this Policy ... where the Exceptional Dealing Approval Request is accompanied by sufficient evidence that the proposed dealing in Telstra securities is the only reasonable course of action available in the circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only theoretical route to a funded collar for a Designated Person is a hardship-type approval showing the collar is the only reasonable course, which is unlikely for a discretionary monetisation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buying and selling Telstra securities within a 3-month period and entering into short term arrangements such as forward contracts in respect of Telstra securities will always be considered speculative dealing and accordingly is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a non-hedging restructure using a forward is deemed speculative, closing off prepaid-forward alternatives to a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: can be withdrawn at any time before you deal if new information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances ... Any such refusal is confidential and you must not disclose the fact that your request has been refused to any other person without the consent of the Telstra Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Where any approval is obtained, the bank may not be told of a refusal or withdrawal, and the executive must execute within 2 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement of which you or any of the persons referred to in (a) or (b) are a beneficiary
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or a trust of which the executive is a beneficiary does not escape the hedging and collateral bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Telstra CEO and Group Executives should undertake any dealings in Telstra securities in compliance with the minimum shareholding requirement (MSR) set out in the Minimum Shareholding Requirement Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A separate MSR policy may treat hedged or encumbered shares as not counting toward the holding requirement; it should be reviewed alongside this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not deal if your proposed dealing could be perceived by the market as you taking advantage of your position in an inappropriate way.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Applies to everyone including non-Designated staff, so even a permitted collar for a Band C executive must survive a market-perception test.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where any Telstra securities granted to a Designated Person under an equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan (for example, Telstra securities that are acquired following the exercise of options or rights or that are released from restriction), the Designated Person must only deal in those Telstra securities in accordance with this Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vested plan shares become ordinary holdings subject to the full hedging and collateral bans once released, so there is no plan-based carve-out for collaring them.

TLS.summary: A funded collar is not possible for Telstra Designated Persons, which covers all directors, the company secretary, all Band A and B executives (including all executive KMP), direct reports of Band A executives and their Closely Related Parties. Paragraph 19 prohibits any hedging arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Telstra securities, vested or unvested, and paragraph 16(b) separately prohibits using Telstra securities as collateral in any financial transaction, so both the option legs and the secured loan are banned outright with no window-period or approval route. The only openings are an arrangement entered before the person became a Designated Person, which may continue for up to 12 months (loan) or a Company Secretary-approved limited period (hedge), and an Exceptional Dealing Approval in severe hardship or under court order where the dealing is the only reasonable course of action. Employees who are not Designated Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and market perception obligation, except that equity plan participants (Band C executives) may not hedge plan securities before vesting, exercise or release from trading restriction.

WOW.summary: A funded collar is not possible for Woolworths Specified Persons (directors, Executives, their direct reports, General Managers and designated roles, together with their Closely Related Parties) because section 4.1 prohibits any new arrangement using Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction after 20 August 2021, with no approval or exemption route. An unfunded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is achievable: collars are expressly Derivatives and hedging of vested unrestricted Securities is permitted with prior written clearance from the Schedule 1 approver (Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee for the Chair; Chair for directors, CEO and CLO; CEO for Executives; Company Secretary or CLO for others), valid five business days, outside the four Blackout Periods running from the 20th of the last month of each quarter. Derivatives over unvested or disposal-restricted Securities are banned for all Team Members, shares cannot be sold within three months of purchase, creating a security interest is itself a Trade, and Directors' and Executives' trades must be reported to the Company Secretary within two days, with Woolworths free to publicly disclose a Director's Derivative positions.

Sections 4.1 to 4.5 (insider trading, waiting period, tipping, stop-loss orders, speculative transactions including puts, calls and short sales) apply to Insiders and their household members, controlled entities and trusts.

Reporting and 16(b) extend to household family members and trusts, corporations or partnerships the person controls.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from engaging in any speculative transactions involving ResMed Securities, including: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is a purchased put and a written call, so both option legs are expressly prohibited for Insiders regardless of whether the shares are vested, the venue is OTC, or the purpose is protective rather than speculative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any transaction involving ResMed Securities (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition), must first obtain pre-approval of the transaction from the Global General Counsel
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pledging shares to the bank and any non-option hedge are clearable transactions for Specified Persons, so the loan leg is possible with approval even though the option legs are not; approval must be sought at least two business days ahead.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval for a proposed transaction may be withheld ... if ... the transaction could result in adverse publicity or have a material adverse impact on trading in ResMed Securities or ResMed; for persons subject to Section 16 ... the transaction could result in liability to the Specified Person under the short-swing rules of Section 16(b); or sufficient advance notice had not been given to allow preparation and review of a Form 4
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a permitted pledge or hedge can be refused on reputational or Section 16(b) grounds, and a refusal cannot be overruled by management.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance, when given, will be only for the precise period specified. ... It is incumbent on the Specified Person to stop any such order that extends beyond the permitted period, or when the Specified Person comes into possession of material non-public information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared transaction must be executed within the stated period and abandoned if inside information arises, so a multi-step financing cannot rely on a standing approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from placing any "stop loss" orders or any other "limit order" involving ResMed Securities, except pursuant to a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Price-triggered mechanics such as knock-outs, automatic top-up sales or lender liquidation instructions could be characterised as prohibited stop-loss or limit orders unless housed in a pre-approved 10b5-1 plan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Apart from these five exceptions, listed in a through e of this paragraph, there shall be no exceptions to the foregoing prohibitions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no hardship, court-order or lender-enforcement relief, so any sale or settlement outside a trading window is a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Total sales of ResMed common stock by a covered individual for any three-month period may not exceed the greater of: (i) 1% of the total number of outstanding shares ... or (ii) the average weekly reported volume ... The shares must be sold either in a "broker's transaction" or in a transaction directly with a "market maker."
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical delivery of shares to the bank on exercise or enforcement by a director or executive officer is an affiliate sale subject to Rule 144 volume limits, manner-of-sale rules and Form 144 filing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: require our Section 16 Persons to report all transactions involving ResMed Securities (including options, warrants, and other "derivative securities") to the SEC. Almost all transactions must be reported within two business days after the transaction date.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any derivative or pledge-related transaction by a director or executive officer becomes public on Form 4 within two business days and may be matched against other trades within six months for short-swing profit disgorgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you could receive permission to buy a security, but later be refused permission to sell it (at least temporarily). These situations are frequently beyond the control of ResMed, and could lock you into an unwanted investment for a considerable period of time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: ResMed disclaims responsibility if a later clearance to sell or unwind is refused, so the executive bears the liquidity risk of being unable to settle or restructure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An Employee includes an Employee's spouse, children, or relatives in the same household; corporation or other business entity controlled by an Employee, or trust in which the Employee acts as trustee or has a beneficial or pecuniary interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy may be amended or supplemented at any time by our Global General Counsel, Chief Executive Officer or Chief Financial Officer and that any such amendments or supplements will become effective immediately.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The rules governing an outstanding financing can change without notice or Board process during the life of the arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You will only be allowed to purchase or sell ResMed Securities during a trading window period commencing one (1) full trading day following the date of our public disclosure of the financial results
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 5 does not say whether it binds all Employees or only Insiders, but for directors and executives it plainly applies and the Global General Counsel may refuse clearance whenever the window is not in effect.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In accordance with Listing Rule 12.9, which is due to take effect from 1 January 2011, we submit a copy of the Company's current Insider Trading Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the December 2010 lodgement of a May 2010 policy; the current ResMed policy should be checked before relying on these terms.

RMD.summary: A funded collar is not possible in its standard form for ResMed directors and executive officers. Section 4.5 expressly prohibits Insiders (any Employee with access to material non-public information, which captures all directors and executive officers and their household members, controlled entities and trusts) from buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities as speculative transactions, so both option legs are banned regardless of vesting or venue, with no hardship or discretionary exemption other than the power of the Global General Counsel, CEO or CFO to amend the Policy. The loan leg is not banned: a pledge, loan or hedge is a transaction that Specified Persons (directors, executive officers, senior management) may undertake with discretionary pre-approval from the Global General Counsel (or CFO), requested at least two business days ahead, inside a trading window that opens one full trading day after quarterly results and runs at least three weeks, and valid only for the precise period specified. A non-option hedge such as a forward or swap could in theory be pre-approved but faces Section 16(b) six-month short-swing matching, Rule 144 affiliate sale limits, Form 4 disclosure within two business days and the ban on stop-loss and limit orders outside a Rule 10b5-1 plan. Note that this is a 2010-vintage policy and current terms should be verified.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, members of the Executive Committee and their Related Parties must not enter into hedging arrangements in relation to Transurban Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The option legs of a collar are a hedging arrangement and are absolutely prohibited for directors, Executive Committee members and their Related Parties over vested and unvested securities alike.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not obtain margin loans using Transurban Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Transurban Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited for every Employee and Related Party, so a funded collar fails for all tiers regardless of whether the hedge itself is permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may hedge against vested Transurban Securities that are not subject to a holding lock if the hedge is both initiated in, and arranged so that the specified exercise date falls within, an Open Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For Employees below Executive Committee level an unfunded collar must be executed in an Open Period with a fixed expiry inside an Open Period, which effectively requires European-style options and rules out American exercise or early termination rights that could fall in a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging is a form of dealing. Therefore, where hedging is not prohibited under this Policy it must be undertaken in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A permitted hedge by a Restricted Person needs prior approval, is subject to Closed Periods and must be reported to the Company Secretary within two ASX trading days as a 'hedge'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where an Employee ... has a hedge which is to be exercised in an Open Period but the Transurban Board has decided to declare or extend a Closed Period to cover the exercise date, the Employee may request prior approval to exercise
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Settlement of a permitted employee hedge can be blocked by a later Closed Period and depends on discretionary approval, a risk the bank should price into settlement mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: I will not engage in short selling of Transurban Securities, obtain margin loans using Transurban Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for loans or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Transurban Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every approval request requires a personal undertaking against secured financing, so a funded collar would involve a false acknowledgement as well as a policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a person or company that has a private understanding or business arrangement with the person for dealing in Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A counterparty or vehicle with a standing arrangement to deal in Transurban Securities on the executive's behalf may itself be a Related Party, so the bans cannot be avoided by interposing an entity or nominee.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a request for approval to trade is granted, it may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in the circumstances of Transurban Securities. If a request for approval to trade is refused, the decision is final and binding and the Employee who has sought the clearance must keep the information (of the refusal) confidential
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved dealing can be revoked before execution within its five-trading-day validity and the executive may not tell the bank why a request was refused.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may be granted prior approval to sell or otherwise deal in Transurban Securities during a Closed Period or on a short term basis
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closed Period relief extends to any dealing, not just sales, but is confined to hardship, court order or other exceptional circumstances and cannot override the hedging or secured financing bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the shares in THL, the shares in TIL and the units in THT stapled together and quoted on the ASX; and any other Securities relating to Transurban.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any hedge or security would need to cover the stapled triple security as a unit, and 'any other Securities relating to Transurban' sweeps in OTC option contracts.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not, except in exceptional circumstances (see section 5.7), deal in Transurban Securities during the following periods (Closed Periods)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a counterparty's enforcement or physical settlement in a Closed Period, so even a permitted employee hedge must avoid settlement or unwind in the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods.

TCL.summary: A funded collar is not possible under Transurban's policy for any tier. Section 5.6 prohibits every Employee and their Related Parties from margin loans and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Transurban Securities, with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, so the loan secured on the collared shares is barred outright; each dealing request also requires a signed acknowledgement not to enter such arrangements. For directors, Executive Committee members and their Related Parties the option legs are independently prohibited by the absolute hedging ban in section 5.5. An unfunded collar over vested, unlocked securities is available only to Employees below Executive Committee level (including their direct reports as Restricted Persons, who need prior Company Secretary approval valid five ASX trading days) if it is initiated in an Open Period with the specified exercise date falling in an Open Period, outside the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods, reported to the Company Secretary within two ASX trading days, and not over unvested or holding-locked equity plan entitlements.

tiers.name: Employees

Subject to the section 3 restrictions: no dealing with Inside Information or after a company no-deal notice, hedging bans on unvested/locked plan securities, and the short-term/speculative/short-selling bans. No approval or blackout regime unless also a Designated Person.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Non-executive directors (including directors-elect), all members of the Executive Steering Committee and their direct reports (Senior Executives), and Nominated Employees advised by the Company Secretary. Subject to blackout periods, prior written approval for every dealing, the margin lending ban and the Connected Persons obligation.

tiers.name: Non-executive Directors

ESC members are approved by the CEO (the CEO by the Chair) and must confirm compliance with the Executive Minimum Shareholding Policy; direct reports are approved by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Other persons who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to the Designated Person restrictions; approved by the Company Secretary.

Designated Persons must ensure they only deal when the Designated Person could, and should obtain clearance for their dealings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Aristocrat will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on collared shares with LVR triggers or lender sale rights risks being treated as a 'margin lending arrangement' banned for Designated Persons even if not so labelled.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not: (a) enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Aristocrat securities; or (b) transfer securities in Aristocrat into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending; a fixed-term, non-margin secured loan is not expressly prohibited, so the loan leg turns on whether the facility has margin-call mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Aristocrat securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is squarely hedging, so it is barred over unvested plan securities and shares under a holding lock, and permitted only over vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with tenor under three months or early-termination features may be characterised as a short-term dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval of a collar over executive shareholdings is discretionary and may be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 business days and approval can be withdrawn before signing; the bank cannot be told why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A request for approval under sections 4.2 or 4.3 by members of the Executive Steering Committee must be accompanied by a confirmation that the member is in compliance with the Executive Minimum Shareholding Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: ESC members must show MSR compliance before a collar is approved; whether collared shares count toward the MSR is governed by the external policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or any other entity which the Designated Person has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a controlled entity or family trust does not avoid the approval requirement, blackouts or the margin lending ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Aristocrat securities which are placed but not completed outside of a blackout period ... must be completed within 5 trading days of the order being placed otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement or unwind of a collar that straddles the start of a blackout is not accommodated; settlement dates should avoid blackout periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach caused by the collar or the lender's enforcement could result in forfeiture of the collared securities, a risk to the bank's collateral.

ALL.summary: A funded collar is possible for a Designated Person (non-executive director, ESC member or direct report) over vested shares that are not subject to a plan holding lock, but only with prior written approval routed through the Company Secretary to the CEO, Chair of the Board, Chair of the Audit Committee or Company Secretary as applicable, executed within 5 business days, outside the 30 September, 31 March and pre-AGM blackouts, and satisfying the Front Page Test. The put and call legs are 'hedging' under the policy's broad definition, so they cannot cover unvested plan securities or locked shares; ESC members must also confirm compliance with the Executive Minimum Shareholding Policy. The loan leg is only expressly restricted as a 'margin lending arrangement' (Designated Persons may neither enter one nor transfer shares into a margin account), so a fixed-term loan without margin-call mechanics is not expressly barred, but the stated substance-over-form approach makes a facility with LVR triggers or lender sale rights likely to be treated as margin lending. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban, which names forward contracts, and any unwind or settlement is a further dealing requiring fresh approval.
