rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include derivatives of shares, including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash or physically settled. Trading in them at any time requires prior written clearance from the Approving Officer and is barred in Prohibited Periods absent exceptional circumstances.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration scheme; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of the person's security holding is expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under Section 7. The policy does not distinguish vested-but-locked shares; release from holding lock is an excluded dealing but hedging locked shares is not separately addressed.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of securities (a trade) and, insofar as it limits economic risk or is secured on the shares, falls under the clearance regimes in Sections 9 and 10.
rules.evidence: To "trade" in securities means, whether as principal or agent, to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities; or enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the trade definition.
CFDs are not named but cash-settled derivatives and equity swaps over Company shares are Company Securities, so a CFD is a trade requiring prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loan agreements over Company Securities are permitted with prior written clearance from the Approving Officer. A disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a margin lending arrangement is excluded from the blackout restrictions.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 7.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage or pledge is not named as such, but any 'secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities' requires prior written clearance, which captures a security interest granted to a lender. A charge unconnected with lending is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance

rules.detail: Any secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities is permitted with prior written clearance; no vesting-state carve-out is stated. A lender's enforcement disposal is an excluded trade for blackout purposes.

rules.detail: No short-term, speculative or minimum holding-period rule; the Approving Officer may consider reputational implications when clearing.

NST.summary: A funded collar over vested shares is possible for a Restricted Person under this policy, subject to clearance. Hedging of a person's security holding (Section 9) and margin loans or other secured lending arrangements over Company Securities (Section 10) are each expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (Company Secretary for Senior Employees and consultants; Executive Chairman for non-director KMP; Executive Chairman and Lead Independent Director jointly for non-executive directors), who must take General Counsel advice and may withdraw clearance at any time; clearance is valid for 5 business days. Hedging of unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements is absolutely prohibited, and OTC options and cash-settled derivatives are expressly Company Securities so every entry, unwind or settlement is a trade needing fresh clearance and cannot occur in the half-year, full-year and quarterly Blackout Periods or a confidential Additional Period absent exceptional circumstances. A lender's enforcement disposal is an excluded trade for blackout purposes. There is no short-term dealing rule or minimum shareholding requirement, and no express disclosure obligation for the financing beyond directors' notification of holding changes.

rules.detail: The derivative definition expressly names options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars and any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding securities; derivatives (cash or physically settled, including third-party products) are QBE securities. rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward is a forward contract limiting economic risk (hedging, banned) and any structure secured on QBE securities is a prohibited secured financial arrangement.

QBE.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any director, executive or employee. Hedging of QBE securities, defined to include any transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding them, is prohibited at all times for all Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties, and 'collars' are expressly named in the derivative definition, so the put and call legs are banned over vested and unvested shares alike. The loan leg is independently prohibited: paragraph 4.2(c) bars margin lending, transfers into margin accounts and any pledging, collateralisation or use of QBE securities as security for any financing arrangement, and granting a mortgage or other right over securities is a dealing. The paragraph 5 waiver power extends only to Closed Periods and the three-month short-term dealing rule, not to hedging or secured financing, and there is no other exemption authority. Paragraph 6 persons (directors, GEC members and their direct reports, divisional board directors and EMB members) need written clearance, valid for 5 business days, for any other dealing at any time.

COL.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a director or Executive Leadership Team member: section 6.3(a) absolutely prohibits them and their Connected Persons from hedging any exposure to Company securities, and section 6.2 bars all Restricted Persons from any secured financing arrangement in respect of Company securities, including margin loans, transfers into margin accounts and sales to meet margin calls, with no waiver authority. For Permitted Restricted Persons (General Manager level and above, nominated team members) the put and call legs over vested, unrestricted shares are permitted as a cleared dealing with written approval from the Company Secretary (confirmed with two Disclosure Committee members), executed within two clear trading days outside the 20 June, 20 December, 1 April and 1 October blackouts, but the loan secured on those shares remains prohibited, so only an unfunded collar is available to them. Plan securities can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, and forward contracts are named as short-term dealings so tenor should exceed three months. Team members below Restricted Person level are outside sections 5 and 6 and could enter a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares subject only to insider trading law.

Only 'margin loan arrangements' are named, but the ban extends to any such arrangement 'in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment' and the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) applies to any loan secured on Sigma Shares. Section 11 separately bars arrangements that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquisition. A non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed.

SIG.exemption_authority: Chairman (CEO for the Chairman) may grant special dispensation to trade in a prohibited period for extraordinary circumstances, exercised sparingly, with legal advice available at Sigma's expense and evidence required; the Chairman also approves clearance timeframes beyond two business days. Board approves the Policy and can prohibit dealing at other times.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Sigma Shares ...: put or call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars and any other hedging or investment arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar is squarely a Derivative and, through the Sigma Shares definition, a dealing in Sigma Shares requiring Chairman clearance and subject to Closed Periods and the unvested/holding-lock ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested, provided any dealing in those derivatives complies with the other requirements of this policy and the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no general hedging ban for directors or executives; the put and call legs over vested, unlocked shares are expressly contemplated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Team Members are prohibited from entering margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Sigma Shares or in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is caught if characterised as a margin loan arrangement; the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) means a bank facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely treated the same way.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members who acquire Sigma Shares must not dispose of those shares, or enter arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those shares being disposed of, within 12 months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with physical settlement or a secured loan with enforcement rights over shares acquired within the past 12 months is a prohibited arrangement; the collar should cover only shares held (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares acquired) at least 12 months earlier or fall within the carve-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members are prohibited from entering short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot borrow the collared shares from the executive to hedge its own position or to structure the facility as a securities loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Team Member means any full time, part time or casual employee of any member of Sigma Group and extends to any secondee, contractor or consultant of, or adviser to, any member of Sigma Group whose terms of engagement require them, or who have been given written notice ... to comply with this policy as though they were an employee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Sections 11 and 12 (12-month holding, derivatives, margin loans) are addressed to Team Members, so their application to non-executive Directors, who are Specified Persons but not employees, depends on their engagement terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No clearance to trade will be given during a Closed Period as these are periods when the risk of insider trading, or the appearance of insider trading is high.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar must all fall in open periods; only the Chairman's extraordinary-circumstances dispensation can override this.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for two business days ... Timeframes beyond 2 days require the approval of the Sigma Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar must be priced and executed within two business days of clearance unless the Chairman approves a longer window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade should not be granted where: there is a matter in relation to which inside information in respect of Sigma Shares (whether the Specified Person knows about the matter or not) when the Specified Person requests clearance or proposes to deal in Sigma Shares
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be refused without reasons because of a matter the executive is unaware of, and refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the blocking of off market dealings for Specified Persons where shares are held through issuer sponsored holdings without prior clearance ... monitor all trades by Specified Person via share registry trading alerts
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Transfer of issuer-sponsored shares to a bank custodian or nominee will be blocked at the registry without clearance and any movement will be flagged to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The additional restrictions on Specified Persons in Chapter 4 do not apply to dealing by a Specified Person or their Associate that constitutes or involves, or results directly from, any of the acts or circumstances set out below.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The section 17 exceptions relieve only the clearance requirement, not the Closed Period, 12-month or margin loan rules, and there is no secured-lender enforcement exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company, trust or other entity that A or any of their family members referred to above controls (whether alone or jointly with each other)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered through a family trust or controlled company is treated as the Specified Person's own dealing and needs clearance.

SIG.summary: The collar legs are available but the loan leg is doubtful. Derivatives, with collars and OTC put and call options expressly named, may be used over vested Sigma Shares that are not under a holding lock, so a director or executive who is a Specified Person can enter the put and call with prior written clearance from the Chairman (CEO for the Chairman), valid for two business days, outside the 31 July, 31 January and pre-AGM Closed Periods, with post-trade confirmation within three business days. Derivatives over unvested shares are absolutely prohibited, stock lending and short selling are banned, and no arrangement that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquiring the shares is permitted, so the collar should cover shares held for at least 12 months (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares). The loan secured on the collared shares is caught by section 12 if it is a 'margin loan arrangement in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security'; the policy's stated concern is lender-compelled sales in Closed Periods, so a facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely prohibited, while a non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed and would need the Chairman's clearance. Sections 11 and 12 are addressed to Team Members, leaving their application to non-executive Directors to their engagement terms.

ORG.exemption_authority: None. Dealing during a Closed Period or Additional Prohibition 'will not be permitted' (8.2) and there is no hardship or discretionary waiver; the Board approves only material changes to the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A sale of your Origin Securities by a third party outside your control (such as a margin lender) in a Closed Period or when you are otherwise prohibited by this Policy is a serious breach of this Policy and may result in dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a secured facility existed, the bank's enforcement or physical settlement of the collar during a Closed Period would put the executive in serious breach, so the structure cannot rely on lender enforcement rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: From the date of this Policy, you must not ... enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly prohibited for all personnel and Associates regardless of vesting state, with no approval route; the wording is prospective only and is silent on unwinding pre-existing arrangements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing in Origin Securities during a Closed Period or Additional Prohibitions will not be permitted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No hardship or exceptional-circumstances exemption exists, so collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement must fall entirely within open windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you come to possess Inside Information after receiving clearance to Deal, you must not complete the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within the 2-business-day validity and can become unexecutable if inside information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you hold Origin Securities, you must recognise that a prohibition may apply at the time you wish to sell them, and Origin will have no responsibility to you.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed Additional Prohibitions can block delivery or unwind of shares under the collar at any time, and the executive bears that risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not ... enter into arrangements which result in short-term Dealing (such as margin loans) to minimise the perception of speculative trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or one with early-termination triggers may be characterised as an arrangement resulting in short-term Dealing, so tenor should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy also extends to Associates of Origin Personnel. ... a company, partnership or trust over which: (i) you have control or significant influence
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the secured financing ban or clearance requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: ... any financial product; derivatives ... Dealing: ... create a derivative over Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank is squarely a Dealing subject to clearance and windows.

ORG.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The unfunded derivative legs (purchased put and written call) over vested shares are a Dealing that Directors may enter with prior written clearance from the Chairman and Company Secretary (Manager and Company Secretary for ELT and their direct reports), executed within 2 business days, outside the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods and any confidential Additional Prohibition, and not over plan securities that remain unvested or subject to performance hurdles. However, section 7.1 expressly bans margin lending and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Origin Securities for all personnel and their Associates, with no exemption authority, so a loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright. A lender's forced sale in a Closed Period is a serious breach that may lead to dismissal, and there is no hardship relief. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban, and any unwind or settlement is itself a Dealing requiring fresh clearance.
